entry.title: A Missing Distinction in PO Output: Why Changed Purchase Orders Deserve Their Own Email Template
entry.content:
Clear communication with suppliers is a critical success factor in procurement processes. In SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud, email output plays a central role in informing suppliers about new Purchase Orders as well as subsequent changes.

SAP provides the app Maintain Email Templates, which allows to standardize and streamline email communication. While this functionality is highly valuable, a closer look at Purchase Order output reveals a gap that can lead to confusion on the supplier side.

At the moment, the same predelivered email template is used for both new Purchase Orders and changed Purchase Orders. This blog post explains why this is problematic, outlines a proposed enhancement, and highlights the business benefits of introducing a dedicated email template for PO changes.

The Current Situation

In the app Maintain Email Templates (F1306A), users can create custom email templates by copying predelivered ones.

For Purchase Orders, SAP currently delivers only one standard template: “Purchase Order Default Email Template” (MM_PUR_PO_DEFAULT_TEMPLATE)

This template is used for both:

1️⃣  Initial Purchase Order output

2️⃣  Changed Purchase Order output

 

From the system’s perspective, the distinction between a new PO and a changed PO exists - the output messages contain a Change Indicator.

 

However, this distinction is not reflected in the email body sent to suppliers.

As a result, the only indication that a PO has been changed can typically be found inside the attached PDF, not in the email itself.

Why This Is a Problem

From a supplier’s point of view, email notifications are often processed quickly - sometimes automatically, sometimes manually.

When a changed Purchase Order uses the same email wording as a new one, several issues may arise:

  • Suppliers may assume a new order instead of a change
  • Important changes may be overlooked
  • Duplicate deliveries may occur if the “change of” note in the PDF is missed

In short: the lack of a clear distinction in the email text can lead to misinterpretation and operational risks.

The Opportunity for Improvement

The enhancement opportunity is both simple and logical:

Provide a predelivered email template specifically for Changed Purchase Orders.

Since the system already knows whether a message relates to:

  • a new Purchase Order, or
  • a changed Purchase Order (via the Change Indicator),

this information could be used as a trigger to:

  • Select a dedicated predelivered template for PO changes
  • Allow customers to create custom templates based on this distinction

 

This approach would align email output behavior with the actual business context of the message.

Expected Business Benefits

Introducing a specific email template for changed Purchase Orders would deliver immediate value:

✅Clearer supplier communication
Suppliers instantly understand that an existing order has been updated.

✅Greater process stability
Reduced risk of misunderstandings and follow‑up corrections.

✅Prevention of duplicate deliveries
Especially critical when quantity or schedule changes are involved.

✅Improved professionalism of external communication
Emails reflect the real business intent, not just the attached document.

Why This Matters

Email output is often the first and sometimes only touchpoint between SAP and suppliers. If that message is ambiguous, even accurate PDFs may not compensate for the initial confusion.

Given that:

  • SAP already distinguishes between new and changed POs internally, and
  • Business Users can already maintain flexible email templates,

introducing a dedicated predelivered template for PO changes would be a natural and consistent next step.

Sometimes, improving a process does not require new functionality - just a better use of the information already available.

Call to Action

If you agree that Changed Purchase Orders should have their own predelivered email template, 

👉   Please Vote to Idea # 372777 Specific Email Template for Change of Purchase Order on SAP Influence and help move this enhancement forward.

entry.title: Use BAdi implemenetation to update unsupported fields in mass changes to Enterprise Project
entry.content:
Currently, not all of the fields in enterprise projects and WBS Elements are supported with mass change function. BAdi implementation on determination can be used as a workaround.

In this article, let's take PSM field 'Budget availability control' as an example. This field is not supported in the Fiori App Mass Change to Projects. While it is exposed in the BAdi implementation /S4PPM/PROJECT_DETERMINATION.

 

Here is the BAdi implementation, the check logic will be triggered if the priority code is updated as '003' (Medium). If it is, then the BAdi will update the target field WbsIsAvailyControlObj(Budget availability control) as abap_true.

IF enterpriseproject-prioritycode = '003' and enterpriseproject-wbsisavailycontrolcontrolobj IS INITIAL.
    changedenterpriseproject-wbsisavailycontrolcontrolobj = abap_true.
ENDIF.

 

As this is triggered at the determination stage, so all of the original determination and validation checks will still work as expected.

The trigger field and target field can be replaced by any other fields. But for the trigger field, it is better to be a convertiable field and its update should not trigger any other business scenario.

 

Then schedule a mass change job to update the prioirt code for any enterprise project.

The trigger field priority and the traget field AVC check level are both updated after the mass change job is executed successfully.

entry.title: SAP S/4HANA DRC: Extending the Canada GST/HST Report to Enable Optional Tax Lines (90, 91, 102).
entry.content:
Introduction

If your organization files a GST/HST return with the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), you are likely familiar with the standard lines on Form GST34 (the amounts you collect, the credits you claim, and the net tax you remit or recover). While most businesses complete the core required lines and submit, the CRA form also includes optional revenue classification lines (Lines 90, 91, and 102) that allow businesses to break down their total revenue into more specific categories. These lines are used by organizations that deal with a mix of supply types, such as: 

  • Standard taxable sales (e.g., most goods and services subject to GST/HST)
  • Zero-rated supplies (e.g., basic groceries, prescription drugs, exports)
  • Exempt supplies (e.g., residential rents, financial services)
  • Other revenue (e.g., goodwill, sale of capital real property, supplies made outside Canada)

 While these lines are optional for many businesses, some organizations, particularly those in financial services, real estate, or with cross-border operations, may need or choose to complete them.

This blog provides a comprehensive guide to configuring these three additional tax boxes to the standard Canada GST/HST DRC report using the DRC extensibility framework. The process does not require any ABAP development, as all steps are accomplished within the scope of Key User extensibility, thereby ensuring the system remains fully upgrade-safe.

Background: Standard Report Architecture

The report relies on two key DRC queries:

1. BOX_SUMM: This query:

  • Reads all posted tax documents and their tax box mappings
  • Summarizes tax code values (tax amount and base amount) against their respective tax boxes
  • Prepares source data for the following standard tax boxes: GST_101, GST_103, GST_104, GST_106, GST_107, GST_110, GST_111, GST_135, GST_136, GST_205, GST_405

2. DERIVED_FIELDS: This query applies formula-based calculations on top of the BOX_SUMM output, using ABAP class CL_FICA_VAT_ACR_DERIVEDFIELDS, method GST_REP

 Note on DERIVED_FIELDS: No changes are required to the DERIVED_FIELDS query. Boxes 90, 91, and 102 are direct summary (source) boxes — their values are derived purely from tax code mappings and carry no formula dependency with other boxes. This significantly simplifies the extension.

 

What Needs to Change

To add support for tax boxes 090, 091, and 102, the following areas require configuration and extension:

  1. Create new tax codes (if required)
  2. Tax box mapping
  3. DRC Query extension
  4. DRC Output schema extension

Step 1 — Create Tax Codes

Configure Your Solution → Finance → Tax on Sales/Purchases → Tax Codes → Define Tax Codes for Sales and Purchases (SSCUI 101016)

Create one tax code for each box: GST_090, GST_091, and GST_102. Use a consistent naming convention that clearly identifies the purpose of each code. Example names: S3 (→ GST_090), S4 (→ GST_091), S5 (→ GST_102).

For standard taxable supply reporting (Line 90), use the applicable GST rate (5%) or HST rate (13%–15% depending on province). entry.title: Header-to-Item Custom Field Copy in S/4HANA Cloud Service using CRMS4_SERV_CUST_H_MODIFY / I_MODIFY
entry.content:
In SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition (2602), I had a Service Management requirement that looked trivial on paper and turned into a nice little tour of the extensibility layers: the user enters a Customer Reference only at the service document header, and that value has to be copied down to a custom field at item level automatically. This post walks through why the obvious BAdIs don't get you there on their own, how to confirm developer extensibility is open to you, and the full working implementation including the gotchas that cost me time.

The requirement

Using key user extensibility (Custom Fields app), I created two text custom fields and exposed them on the Manage Service Contracts app via Adapt UI:

  • Header field Customer Reference on business context Service Header (CRMS4_SERV_H). Its persistence component resolved to YY1_CUSTOMERREFERENCE_SRH.
  • Item field Customer Reference Item on business context Service Item (CRMS4_SERV_I).

Both save and display correctly from the UI. The business rule: the user only maintains the header value, and the item field should mirror it without manual entry.

The BAdIs I planned to use

The enhancement spot for service one-order is ES_S4CRM_1O_EXTENSION, which contains, among others:

  • CRMS4_SERV_CUST_H_MODIFY (Service Document Header Modifications) — importing SERVICEHEADER, SERVICEHEADER_EXTENSION_IN; changing SERVICEHEADER_EXTENSION_OUT.
  • CRMS4_SERV_CUST_I_MODIFY (Service Document Item Modifications) — importing SERVICEHEADER, SERVICEITEM, SERVICEITEM_EXTENSION_IN; changing SERVICEITEM_EXTENSION_OUT.

My first instinct was: read the header value in the item BAdI and write it to the item extension field. Simple.

Why that falls short (and why Custom Logic scope can't bridge it)

The item BAdI receives the standard header structure SERVICEHEADER (type CRMS4S_SERV_H_BADI) — but it does not receive the header extension fields. So inside CRMS4_SERV_CUST_I_MODIFY there is no way to read YY1_CUSTOMERREFERENCE from the header. Conversely, the header BAdI has the header custom field but cannot touch items.

So the value lives in one BAdI and has to be written in another. The standard pattern for that is a small in-memory buffer: the header BAdI stashes the value, the item BAdI reads it. The problem with doing this in key user Custom Logic scope is that you can't create a standalone global class or shared object to hold that state, and custom logic can't reference an arbitrary custom class — so a clean cross-header-to-item copy isn't feasible there. That pushed me to developer extensibility.

Checking the API Hub: is it released for Developer Extensibility?

Older SAP Community threads (2024) noted these BAdIs were released only for key user apps (USE_IN_KEY_USER_APPS). Release status changes by release, so check your own. On the SAP Business Accelerator Hub, open the BAdI (Developer Extensibility → BAdIs) and look at the Release State tiles. On 2602, CRMS4_SERV_CUST_I_MODIFY showed Release State Developer Extensibility: Released (and the same for the header BAdI). That's the green light — verify both the header and item definitions before you start.

The approach: developer extensibility + a static buffer bridge

Three things to build: a buffer class to carry the value across the two BAdI calls, plus an implementing class for each BAdI. The header BAdI runs first in the save sequence and fills the buffer; the item BAdI reads it.

Step 1 — Prerequisites

  • Connect ADT to the Development tenant , not the Customizing tenant. Developer extensibility objects can only be created on Development tenant .
  • Have a customer software component and package enabled for ABAP for Cloud Development.

Step 2 — The buffer class

Create and activate this first, since the implementing classes reference it. The key is the document character UUID (SERVICEDOCUMENTCHARUUID), which exists identically on the header and item BAdI's SERVICEHEADER structure and is stable from creation — unlike the document number, which can be empty for a new document.

 
 
abap
CLASS zcl_serv_custref_buf DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    CLASS-METHODS set
      IMPORTING iv_guid  TYPE crms4s_serv_h_badi-servicedocumentcharuuid                iv_value TYPE crms4s_serv_h_incl_eew_ps-yy1_customerreference_srh.
    CLASS-METHODS get
      IMPORTING iv_guid         TYPE crms4s_serv_h_badi-servicedocumentcharuuid      RETURNING VALUE(rv_value) TYPE crms4s_serv_h_incl_eew_ps-yy1_customerreference_srh.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_row,
             guid  TYPE crms4s_serv_h_badi-servicedocumentcharuuid,
             value TYPE crms4s_serv_h_incl_eew_ps-yy1_customerreference_srh,
           END OF ty_row.
    CLASS-DATA gt_buf TYPE SORTED TABLE OF ty_row WITH UNIQUE KEY guid.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_serv_custref_buf IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD set.
    DELETE gt_buf WHERE guid = iv_guid.
    INSERT VALUE #( guid = iv_guid value = iv_value ) INTO TABLE gt_buf.
  ENDMETHOD.
  METHOD get.
    READ TABLE gt_buf WITH KEY guid = iv_guid INTO DATA(ls).
    IF sy-subrc = 0.
      rv_value = ls-value.
    ENDIF.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

Step 3 — Enhancement implementation and BAdI implementations

In ADT: New → Other ABAP Repository Object → Enhancement → Enhancement Implementation, against enhancement spot ES_S4CRM_1O_EXTENSION. Inside that single enhancement implementation you can host both BAdI implementations:

  1. Add BAdI Implementation for BAdI definition CRMS4_SERV_CUST_I_MODIFY (e.g. name ZUPDATE_CUSTREF_H_TO_I), implementing class ZCL_SERV_CUST_I_MODIFY, "Active implementation" ticked.
  2. Add BAdI Implementation for BAdI definition CRMS4_SERV_CUST_H_MODIFY, implementing class ZCL_SERV_CUST_H_MODIFY.

Tip: in the Implementing Class field, type the class name and use the quick-fix (Ctrl+1 → create implementing class) so ADT generates the class already wired to the BAdI interface and the MODIFY method signature.

Step 4 — The header implementing class (fills the buffer)

Read the value from SERVICEHEADER_EXTENSION_OUT first (what the user entered in this interaction); fall back to SERVICEHEADER_EXTENSION_IN (the existing/persisted value) when OUT is empty. This matters — see the gotchas.

 
 
abap
CLASS zcl_serv_cust_h_modify DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    INTERFACES if_crms4_serv_cust_h_modify.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_serv_cust_h_modify IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD if_crms4_serv_cust_h_modify~modify.
    DATA(lv_value) = serviceheader_extension_out-yy1_customerreference_srh.
    IF lv_value IS INITIAL.
      lv_value = serviceheader_extension_in-yy1_customerreference_srh.
    ENDIF.
    zcl_serv_custref_buf=>set(
      iv_guid  = serviceheader-servicedocumentcharuuid      iv_value = lv_value ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

Step 5 — The item implementing class (reads the buffer)

 
 
abap
CLASS zcl_serv_cust_i_modify DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    INTERFACES if_crms4_serv_cust_i_modify.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_serv_cust_i_modify IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD if_crms4_serv_cust_i_modify~modify.
    DATA(lv_ref) = zcl_serv_custref_buf=>get( serviceheader-servicedocumentcharuuid ).
    " confirm your item field's exact component name (context suffix) via code completion
    serviceitem_extension_out-yy1_customerreferenitm_sri = lv_ref.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

Activate the buffer class first, then both implementing classes.

How H_MODIFY and I_MODIFY are triggered

This is the part that's easy to misjudge:

  • The header MODIFY fires whenever the document is saved/touched.
  • The item MODIFY fires per item, only for items that are created or changed in that save — not for untouched items.
  • In the save sequence, the header MODIFY runs before the item MODIFY. That ordering is exactly what makes the buffer work: header sets, item gets.

Consequences:

  • Create a contract with items and a header reference in the same save → both fire → the value copies.
  • Touch an item on an existing contract → the item BAdI fires for that item, reads the buffer (which the header BAdI filled with the current header value via the OUT/IN logic), and copies.
  • Edit only the header reference on an existing contract → the item BAdI does not fire for untouched items, so they won't resync. You cannot flag items as dirty from the header BAdI in this released set, so this is a design boundary to be aware of, not a bug.

Testing and the gotchas

Use the ADT debugger for this (Custom Logic Tracing is for key user logic, not your Z classes). Set breakpoints in both MODIFY methods and run a save from the Fiori UI.

The gotchas that actually bit me:

  1. There is no GUID field on CRMS4S_SERV_H_BADI. The fields use CDS-style names; the usable key is SERVICEDOCUMENTCHARUUID. Don't use the document number — it can be blank for new documents.
  2. Field component names carry a context suffix. The header field resolved to YY1_CUSTOMERREFERENCE_SRH. The item field will have its own suffix (verify with code completion on serviceitem_extension_out-). Get these exact or it won't compile/copy.
  3. Don't write serviceheader_extension_out = serviceheader_extension_in. That line appears in SAP's sample code and overwrites the user's freshly entered value with the old one.
  4. OUT vs IN. In my first test the buffer row existed with the right UUID but a blank VALUE. The reason: I had only changed a line item, not re-entered the header field, so SERVICEHEADER_EXTENSION_OUT came in empty while the actual value sat in SERVICEHEADER_EXTENSION_IN. Reading OUT with an IN fallback (as in Step 4) fixed it and makes the copy robust whether or not the header was touched in that save.
  5. Edit-only-header limitation (above): if the business needs a later header-only change to resync existing items, this in-transaction pattern won't cover it — you'd need an API-driven update that actually touches the items.

Takeaways

The core lesson is that the service item modify BAdI deliberately doesn't expose header extension fields, so any header-to-item copy needs a bridge across the two BAdI calls — a static buffer keyed by the document UUID, populated in the header BAdI and read in the item BAdI. Add to that the OUT/IN value source, the correct UUID key, the context-suffixed field names, and the per-item trigger behavior, and you have a clean, upgrade-stable solution entirely within developer extensibility.

If you've solved the edit-only-header resync cleanly, I'd be glad to hear how in the comments.

entry.title: 在 SAP S/4HANA Cloud 中通过自定义逻辑在创建外向交货单时实现库存数量不足提醒
entry.content:
问题背景

有客户提出需求，由于业务管理要求,希望在创建外向交货单时能够自动检查交货单行项目物料的库存数量是否充足。具体来说，当外向交货单创建保存时，需要检查交货单对应的销售订单行项目物料数量是否大于物料库存数量，如果库存数量不足，则增加一个 Warning 提示该物料库存数量不足。同时，客户希望在使用 API 创建外向交货单时，也能看到对应的 Message。

解决方案

尝试通过自定义逻辑,使用两个 BAdI 的组合方案来满足需求。

分析步骤

1. 确认适用的 BAdI 增强点

首先,我们需要找到合适的 BAdI 增强点来实现库存检查功能。经过分析,发现增强点 LE_SHP_DELIVERY_FINAL_CHECK 可以在交货单保存之前执行最终检查。因此,可以通过这个 BAdI 实现在前台 APP 创建外向交货单时，如果库存数量不足，返回 Warning 消息提醒。

2. 实现前台 APP 的 Warning 提醒

在 BAdI LE_SHP_DELIVERY_FINAL_CHECK 中实现基本的库存检查逻辑：

    CONSTANTS:
    lc_plant    TYPE werks_d VALUE '1310',
    lc_vkorg    TYPE vkorg   VALUE '1310',
    lc_vtweg    TYPE vtweg   VALUE '20',
    lc_spart    TYPE spart   VALUE '00'.

    DATA:
    lv_so_qty    TYPE menge_d,
    lv_stock TYPE menge_d.

    IF documentprocessingmode = 'CREATE'.
      LOOP AT delivery_document_items_in INTO DATA(ls_item) .
      IF ls_item-plant = lc_plant.
      " 读取销售订单行项目的订单数量
      SELECT SINGLE orderquantity
      FROM i_salesorderitem
      WHERE salesorder     = @LS_item-referencesddocument
        AND salesorderitem = @LS_item-referencesddocumentitem
      INTO @LV_so_qty.
      " 读取物料的库存数量
      SELECT SINGLE MATLWRHSSTKQTYINMATLBASEUNIT
      FROM I_STOCKQUANTITYCURRENTVALUE_2( P_DisplayCurrency = 'CNY' )
      WHERE PRODUCT = @LS_item-MATERIAL
      INTO @LV_stock.
      IF sy-subrc <> 0.
        CONTINUE. " No SO item found – skip this delivery item
      ENDIF.
      IF lv_stock < lv_so_qty.
        message-messagetype = 'W'. " saving of the delivery document will be warned
        message-messagetext = |Warning: 该物料库存数量不足|.
        EXIT.
      ENDIF.
      ENDIF.
      ENDLOOP.
    ENDIF.

3. 发现 API 场景的局限性

但是这里的 Warning Message 只能在前台 APP 显示，API 创建的情况下无法看到 Message。因此需要通过替代方案实现。

4. 实现 API 场景的消息提示

为了让 API 创建场景也能看到提示信息，我们采用以下方案：

方案说明：

- 创建一个自定义字段，这个字段可以在 API Response 里看到。我们创建了一个自定义字段
- 使用 BAdI LE_SHP_SAVE_DOCUMENT_PREPARE，这个 BAdI 可以修改表头和行项目级别的标准字段和自定义字段
- 该 BAdI 将在交货单保存到数据库之前被调用

实现代码：

IF DOCUMENTPROCESSINGMODE = 'CREATE'.
CONSTANTS:
  lc_plant  TYPE werks_d VALUE '1310',
  lc_vkorg  TYPE vkorg   VALUE '1310',
  lc_vtweg  TYPE vtweg   VALUE '20',
  lc_spart  TYPE spart   VALUE '00'.

DATA:
  lv_so_qty TYPE menge_d,
  lv_stock TYPE menge_d.

" -------------------------------------------------------
" Step 1: 必须先将输入完整复制到输出（Cloud BAdI 标准做法）
" -------------------------------------------------------
move-corresponding delivery_document_in to delivery_document_out.
delivery_document_items_out = delivery_document_items_in.

" -------------------------------------------------------
" Step 2: 表头组织数据过滤
" 仅对 Sales Org 1310 / DC 20 / Division 00 生效
" -------------------------------------------------------
*CHECK delivery_document_in-salesorganization = lc_vkorg.

" -------------------------------------------------------
" Step 3: 遍历交货单行项目
" -------------------------------------------------------
LOOP AT delivery_document_items_in INTO DATA(ls_item).


  " 跳过无参考销售订单的行项目
*  CHECK ls_item-referencesddocument IS NOT INITIAL.
*  CHECK ls_item-referencesddocumentitem IS NOT INITIAL.

  " 读取销售订单行项目的订单数量
  SELECT SINGLE orderquantity
    FROM i_salesorderitem
    WHERE salesorder     = @LS_item-referencesddocument
      AND salesorderitem = @LS_item-referencesddocumentitem
    INTO @LV_so_qty.
  " 读取物料的库存数量
  SELECT SINGLE MATLWRHSSTKQTYINMATLBASEUNIT
    FROM I_STOCKQUANTITYCURRENTVALUE_2( P_DisplayCurrency = 'CNY' )
    WHERE PRODUCT = @LS_item-MATERIAL
    INTO @LV_stock.
  IF sy-subrc <> 0.
    CONTINUE. " 未找到对应销售订单行项目，跳过
  ENDIF.

  " 比较库存数量与销售订单数量
  IF lv_stock < lv_so_qty.
    " 更新自定义字段
    DELIVERY_DOCUMENT_OUT-yy1_message_dlh = 'Warning: 该物料库存数量不足。'.
  ENDIF.

ENDLOOP.
ENDIF.

5. 使用到的 CDS View

在实现过程中,我们使用了以下 CDS View 来获取所需的数据:

- I_SalesOrderItem: 用于获取销售订单行项目的订单数量,通过销售订单号和行项目号进行查询
- I_StockQuantityCurrentValue_2: 用于获取物料的当前库存数量,提供了物料在不同存储地点的实时库存信息,非常适合用于库存检查场景

6. 测试验证

测试后，上述代码可以满足需求:

- 在前台 APP 创建外向交货单时，如果库存不足，会显示 Warning 消息

 

- 通过 API 创建外向交货单时，自定义字段的值被更改，可以在 Response 的自定义字段中看到库存不足的提示信息

 

结语

通过阅读本文以及之前写过的几篇相似场景的 Blog，希望您已知晓在创建外向交货单时，如何通过自定义逻辑来实现库存数量检查并在不同场景下返回相应的提示消息。

entry.title: Extend Sales Order with Issue Summary by Using BAdI SD_SLS_END_OF_FINALIZE
entry.content:
Background

In previous blogs, we shared how to use the Cloud BAdI to Update Sales Order in Finalize Phase and how to Trigger Sales Order Approval Workflow Based on Profit Margin by using the extensibility tools in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

In this blog, I will share another real business use case where the developer extensibility BAdI SD_SLS_END_OF_FINALIZE is used to automatically maintain a custom field that provides a human-readable summary of current issues on a sales order, right before saving.

Developer Extensibility BAdIs for Sales Documents

Developer extensibility is one of the three extensibility types available in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. Unlike key user extensibility -- which is configuration-based and available to business users -- developer extensibility requires ABAP development skills and is implemented in ABAP Development Tools (ADT). It allows customers to add custom business logic using released, cloud-compliant APIs under a strict C1 contract, ensuring upgrade stability. 

SD_SLS_END_OF_FINALIZE is the first developer-extensibility BAdI defined specifically for the sales order process. It is called at the very end of the Finalize phase, after all standard processing is complete, so the document state it reads (credit status, block status, incompleteness) is final and fully committed. Unlike earlier BAdIs in the finalize sequence, changes made here do not trigger redetermination of dependent values, which makes it ideal for writing derived or summary fields. It can also return messages to the user and, when necessary, prevent the document from being saved.

For a full comparison of all diffferent BAdIs, including when each fires, what it can modify, and its recommended use case, refer to the SAP Help documentation.

Customer Requirement

The Supplier Company XYZ is a wholesale distributor operating across multiple sales organizations. Their inside sales team processes a high volume of orders daily, and order quality is a constant focus: orders must be complete, credit-approved, and free of supply or delivery blocks before they can be fulfilled.

When an order is flagged as “incomplete” in standard SAP, the system only shows the sales order is incomplete with relevant statuses — it does not tell the user which specific fields are missing, unless user opens the sales order to check for details. 

The Company XYZ wants a single, readable field on the sales order — visible in list reports — that surfaces most relevant issues in one place: for example, [CREDIT BLOCK] [DELIVERY BLOCK] [INCOMPLETE: Payment Terms]. This would allow their order management team to triage issues at a glance without opening each order individually. The standard SAP S/4HANA Cloud incompleteness log does not satisfy this requirement because it is only accessible from within the order itself and does not consolidate blocks and missing fields into a single explainable field.

Solution

Let's see how developer extensibility fulfills this requirement.

We will use the developer-extensibility BAdI SD_SLS_END_OF_FINALIZE to evaluate the state of the sales order immediately before saving and write the result into a custom header field called YY1_ISSUE_SUMMARY_SDH. This field will contain a concise, machine-parseable text string summarizing all active issues.

The BAdI SD_SLS_END_OF_FINALIZE belongs to enhancement spot ES_SD_SLS_DEV_EXTEND and fires at the end of the finalize phase — that is, right before a sales document is saved — regardless of whether the trigger is a manual save, an approval workflow update, a credit decision, or any other process. This makes it the ideal hook for maintaining derived fields that should always reflect the current state of the document.

The solution consists of three parts: creating the custom field, implementing the BAdI logic, and verifying the result in the Fiori UI.

Step 1 — Create the custom field

Open the Custom Fields Fiori app and create a new field for the Sales Document business context:

Field name: YY1_ISSUE_SUMMARY_SDH

Enable the field for the sales order UI and publish it. Publishing the field also generates the corresponding control-YY1_ISSUE_SUMMARY_SDH flag in the BAdI interface, which is required to make writes take effect.

Step 2 — Implement the BAdI

Open ADT (ABAP Development Tools) and navigate to enhancement spot ES_SD_SLS_DEV_EXTEND. Create a new BAdI implementation for SD_SLS_END_OF_FINALIZE and implement the method IF_SD_SLS_END_OF_FINALIZE~MODIFY_FIELDS.

Implement following logic to convert issues into custom field as explainable texts.

The method receives two objects: a dataprovider (read-only access to the document) and a dataprocessor (write access to custom fields). First, skip the method body when called in simulation mode -- this avoids side effects during OData simulation API calls:

IF dataprovider->is_simulation_mode( ) = abap_true.

  RETURN.

ENDIF.

Next, read the header fields and derive the flags needed for the summary:

DATA(lv_credit_status)      = dataprovider->get_salesdocument( )-totalcreditcheckstatus.
DATA(lv_head_incomp_status) = dataprovider->get_salesdocument( )-headerdelivincompletionstatus.
DATA(lv_credit_blocked)     = abap_false.

IF lv_credit_status = 'B' OR lv_credit_status = 'C'.
  lv_credit_blocked = abap_true.
ENDIF.

Then retrieve the incompleteness information. The method GET_INCOMPLETENESS_INFO_INTRNL returns all incomplete field entries, with each entry carrying the technical field name (FDNAM) and the item number (POSNR). A POSNR of 000000 indicates a header-level field; any other value is an item-level field.

DATA(lt_incompletion_info) = dataprovider->get_incompleteness_info_intrnl( ).
DATA lv_summary TYPE string.

Build the summary string by appending tokens for each active issue. Credit block comes first, followed by one token per incomplete field. A SWITCH maps each technical field name to a human-readable label; unknown field names fall back to the raw technical name:

IF lv_credit_blocked = abap_true.
  lv_summary = |[CREDIT BLOCK] |.
ENDIF.

LOOP AT lt_incompletion_info INTO DATA(ls_incompl).
  DATA(lv_field_label) = SWITCH string( ls_incompl-fdnam
    WHEN 'AUGRU'   THEN 'Order Reason'
    WHEN 'BSTKD'   THEN 'PO Number'
    WHEN 'BSTDK'   THEN 'PO Date'
    WHEN 'INCO1'   THEN 'Incoterms'
    WHEN 'INCO2_L' THEN 'Incoterms Location'
    WHEN 'KDGRP'   THEN 'Customer Group'
    WHEN 'KTGRD'   THEN 'Account Assignment Group'
    WHEN 'KUNNR'   THEN 'Ship-to Party'
    WHEN 'LIFSK'   THEN 'Delivery Block'
    WHEN 'LPRIO'   THEN 'Delivery Priority'
    WHEN 'PRSDT'   THEN 'Pricing Date'
    WHEN 'ROUTE'   THEN 'Route'
    WHEN 'VKBUR'   THEN 'Sales Office'
    WHEN 'VKGRP'   THEN 'Sales Group'
    WHEN 'VSBED'   THEN 'Shipping Conditions'
    WHEN 'VSTEL'   THEN 'Shipping Point'
    WHEN 'WAERK'   THEN 'Currency'
    WHEN 'WERKS'   THEN 'Plant'
    WHEN 'ZTERM'   THEN 'Payment Terms'
    ELSE ls_incompl-fdnam ).

  IF ls_incompl-posnr = '000000'.
    lv_summary = lv_summary && |[INCOMPLETE: { lv_field_label }] |.
  ELSE.
    lv_summary = lv_summary && |[ITEM { ls_incompl-posnr } INCOMPLETE: { lv_field_label }] |.
  ENDIF.
ENDLOOP.

Finally, truncate to 200 characters and write to the custom field using SET_HEAD_CUSTOM_FIELDS. The control- flag must always be set to IF_ABAP_BEHV=>MK-ON -- only fields with this flag set are actually persisted:

CONDENSE lv_summary.
IF strlen( lv_summary ) > 200.
  lv_summary = lv_summary(200).
ENDIF.


dataprocessor->set_head_custom_fields(
  VALUE #( yy1_issue_summary_sdh         = lv_summary
           control-yy1_issue_summary_sdh = if_abap_behv=>mk-on ) ).

Save and activate the implementation class in ADT. 

Step 3 — Verify in the Fiori UI

Log on as an Internal Sales Representative and open the Manage Sales Orders - Version 2 Fiori app. Create a new sales order and intentionally leave following fields empty, and save the order without completing it:

  • Customer Reference (header)
  • Shipping Point (item 10)
  • Terms of Payment (item 20)

Open the saved order and check the custom field — the Issue Summary field shows below:

Edit the sales order to provide the customer reference, and then Save the sales order. 

Open the sales order after it is saved, the custom field "Issue Summary" is updated accordingly. 

Conclusion

In this blog, we used the BAdI SD_SLS_END_OF_FINALIZE to implement a lightweight but powerful order quality indicator. By reading the document state — credit check status, delivery block status, and the incompleteness log — right before save, and writing the result into a custom header field, we gave the order management team a consolidated, queryable view of every issue on every order. No batch job, no separate report, no custom Fiori app required.

The BAdI SD_SLS_END_OF_FINALIZE is part of the Developer Extensibility framework in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. It is implemented in ABAP Development Tools (ADT) using only released, cloud-compliant APIs (C1 contract), and it fires on every save regardless of the triggering scenario — manual save, approval workflow, credit decision, and more. This makes it a reliable, low-maintenance extension point for derived fields that must always reflect current document state.

Please find other BAdI use cases in the blog Sales Document BAdI Overview, and stay tuned for more custom sales order type use cases, and feel free to submit your requirements through the Customer Influence Portal to help us prioritize our product roadmap.

entry.title: Using Custom Logic in SAP S/4HANA Cloud to Realize Insufficient Stock Quantity at Outbound Deliver
entry.content:
Problem Background

A customer has requested a feature where, due to business management requirements, they want to automatically check whether the stock quantity of materials in outbound delivery line items is sufficient when creating the delivery. Specifically, when an outbound delivery is saved, the system needs to verify if the material quantity in the corresponding sales order line items exceeds the available stock quantity. If stock is insufficient, a Warning message should be displayed indicating the material shortage. Additionally, the customer wants to see the corresponding messages when creating outbound deliveries via API.

Solution

We implemented a custom logic solution using a combination of two BAdIs to meet the requirements.

Analysis Steps

1. Identifying the Appropriate BAdI Enhancement Points

First, we needed to find suitable BAdI enhancement points to implement the stock check functionality. After analysis, we discovered that the enhancement point LE_SHP_DELIVERY_FINAL_CHECK can execute final checks before the delivery is saved. Therefore, this BAdI can be used to return Warning messages when creating outbound deliveries in the frontend APP if stock quantity is insufficient.

2. Implementing Warning Messages for Frontend APP

We implemented basic stock check logic in BAdI LE_SHP_DELIVERY_FINAL_CHECK:

    CONSTANTS:
    lc_plant    TYPE werks_d VALUE '1310',
    lc_vkorg    TYPE vkorg   VALUE '1310',
    lc_vtweg    TYPE vtweg   VALUE '20',
    lc_spart    TYPE spart   VALUE '00'.

    DATA:
    lv_so_qty    TYPE menge_d,
    lv_stock TYPE menge_d.

    IF documentprocessingmode = 'CREATE'.
      LOOP AT delivery_document_items_in INTO DATA(ls_item) .
      IF ls_item-plant = lc_plant.
      " Get Order Quantity of Sales Order Items
      SELECT SINGLE orderquantity
      FROM i_salesorderitem
      WHERE salesorder     = @LS_item-referencesddocument
        AND salesorderitem = @LS_item-referencesddocumentitem
      INTO @LV_so_qty.
      " Get Stock Quantity
      SELECT SINGLE MATLWRHSSTKQTYINMATLBASEUNIT
      FROM I_STOCKQUANTITYCURRENTVALUE_2( P_DisplayCurrency = 'CNY' )
      WHERE PRODUCT = @LS_item-MATERIAL
      INTO @LV_stock.
      IF sy-subrc <> 0.
        CONTINUE. " No SO item found – skip this delivery item
      ENDIF.
      IF lv_stock < lv_so_qty.
        message-messagetype = 'W'. " saving of the delivery document will be warned
        message-messagetext = |Warning: The material has insufficient stock quantity|.
        EXIT.
      ENDIF.
      ENDIF.
      ENDLOOP.
    ENDIF.

3. Discovering API Scenario Limitations

However, this Warning message only displays in the frontend APP. Messages cannot be seen when creating deliveries via API. Therefore, we needed to implement an alternative solution.

4. Implementing Message Display for API Scenarios

To make the messages visible in API creation scenarios, we adopted the following approach:

Solution Details:

- Create a custom field that can be seen in the API Response
- Use BAdI LE_SHP_SAVE_DOCUMENT_PREPARE, which can modify standard and custom fields at both header and line item levels
- This BAdI is called before the delivery is saved to the database

Implementation Code:

IF documentprocessingmode = 'CREATE'.
  CONSTANTS:
    lc_plant  TYPE werks_d VALUE '1310',
    lc_vkorg  TYPE vkorg   VALUE '1310',
    lc_vtweg  TYPE vtweg   VALUE '20',
    lc_spart  TYPE spart   VALUE '00'.

  DATA:
    lv_so_qty TYPE menge_d,
    lv_stock TYPE menge_d.

  " -------------------------------------------------------
  " Step 1: Must first copy complete input to output (Cloud BAdI standard practice)
  " -------------------------------------------------------
  MOVE-CORRESPONDING delivery_document_in TO delivery_document_out.
  delivery_document_items_out = delivery_document_items_in.

  " -------------------------------------------------------
  " Step 2: Header organization data filter
  " Only applies to Sales Org 1310 / DC 20 / Division 00
  " -------------------------------------------------------
  *CHECK delivery_document_in-salesorganization = lc_vkorg.

  " -------------------------------------------------------
  " Step 3: Loop through delivery line items
  " -------------------------------------------------------
  LOOP AT delivery_document_items_in INTO DATA(ls_item).

    " Skip line items without reference sales order
    *CHECK ls_item-referencesddocument IS NOT INITIAL.
    *CHECK ls_item-referencesddocumentitem IS NOT INITIAL.

    " Read order quantity from sales order line item
    SELECT SINGLE orderquantity
      FROM i_salesorderitem
      WHERE salesorder     = @LS_item-referencesddocument
        AND salesorderitem = @LS_item-referencesddocumentitem
      INTO @LV_so_qty.
    " Read material stock quantity
    SELECT SINGLE matlwrhsstkqtyinmatlbaseunit
      FROM i_stockquantitycurrentvalue_2( p_displaycurrency = 'CNY' )
      WHERE product = @LS_item-material
      INTO @LV_stock.
    IF sy-subrc <> 0.
      CONTINUE. " No corresponding sales order line item found, skip
    ENDIF.

    " Compare stock quantity with sales order quantity
    IF lv_stock < lv_so_qty.
      " Update custom field
      delivery_document_out-yy1_message_dlh = 'Warning: Insufficient stock quantity for this material.'.
    ENDIF.

  ENDLOOP.
ENDIF.

5. CDS Views Used

During implementation, we used the following CDS Views to retrieve the required data:

- I_SalesOrderItem: Used to get the order quantity of sales order line items, queried by sales order number and line item number
- I_StockQuantityCurrentValue_2: Used to get the current stock quantity of materials, providing real-time stock information for materials at different storage locations, which is ideal for stock checking scenarios

6. Testing and Validation

After testing, the above code successfully meets the requirements:

- When creating outbound deliveries in the frontend APP, if stock is insufficient, a Warning message is displayed

 

- When creating outbound deliveries via API, the custom field value is updated, and the stock shortage message can be seen in the Response's custom field

 

Conclusion

By reading this article and several similar scenario blogs I've written previously, I hope you now understand how to implement stock quantity checks through custom logic when creating outbound deliveries, and how to return appropriate messages in different scenarios.

Follow this link to see more questions and blog posts related to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Sales: SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition Sales - SAP Community

If you have any suggestions or ideas about this article, please feel free to share them in the comments section. I look forward to exchanging ideas with you. Also, please follow my personal account, and I hope to see you in the next blog post!

entry.title: SAP RAP : Dynamically manipulating fields based on Parent field value.
entry.content:
Step 1: Define Control Fields in CDS View

Create boolean control fields like isAppleBrand, isMaleGender in your CDS view.

define view ZMobileDevice as select from MobileDevice {
  key ID,
  Brand,
  ModelVariant,
  Gender,
  case Brand when 'Apple' then abap_true else abap_false end as isAppleBrand,
  case Gender when 'Male' then abap_true else abap_false end as isMaleGender
}

 

Step 2: Use Annotations for Conditional Visibility

Use @Former Member.Hidden annotation with control fields.

@Former Member.hidden: 'isAppleBrand'
ModelVariant

@UI.hidden: 'isMaleGender'
PregnancyStatus

@UI.hidden: 'isMaleGender'
MaternityLeave

Step 3: Enable Side Effects

Ensure side effects are triggered when the parent field changes. Handle this in Behaviour Definition.

determination setVisibility on modify { field Brand, Model;  }
  side effects { field Brand affects field isAppleBrand; }

 

Step 4: Behaviour Implementation 

METHOD setVisiblity.
    DATA: lt_update TYPE TABLE FOR UPDATE <root view>.

    READ ENTITIES OF <root view> IN LOCAL MODE
        ENTITY <entity>
        FIELDS ( Brand Model )
        WITH CORRESPONDING #( keys )
        RESULT DATA(lt_mob_data).


    DATA lt_update_fields TYPE TABLE FOR UPDATE <root view>.
    DATA ls_update_fields LIKE LINE OF lt_update_fields.

*
data(ls_entity) = lt_mob_data[ 1 ]-entity.


    lt_update = VALUE #( FOR ls_mob IN lt_mob_data (
          %tky = ls_mob-%tky

          " Set the boolean field based on ProjectType
          IsAppleBrand = xsdbool( ls_pir-Brande <> '01' OR ls_pir-Brand IS INITIAL )
         
          " Use the control structure to signal which fields should be updated
          %control = VALUE #(
                              IsAppleBrand = if_abap_behv=>mk-on
                               )
    ) ) ).

    MODIFY ENTITIES OF <rootview> IN LOCAL MODE
         ENTITY <entity>
         UPDATE FROM lt_update
         REPORTED DATA(lt_reported).

    reported = CORRESPONDING #( DEEP lt_reported ).


  ENDMETHOD.

Dynamic field control in SAP RAP enhances user experience by tailoring the UI to the context. Whether you're building a mobile configuration app or a gender-sensitive form, these techniques help you deliver clean, relevant interfaces.

entry.title: SAP Cloud ERP (S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition) 2608亮点前瞻 — 可拓展性 (Extensibility)
entry.content:
大家好，我们即将迎来 SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition 2608 大版本的更新。在本篇博客中，我将会重点展示在 SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition 2608 当中可拓展性部分的亮点更新内容。

API 功能的增强与变更

API 可以帮助我们实现系统间的集成。在 2608 版本，多个 API 都迎来了显著的变更：

高级变式配置 (Advanced Variant Configuration, AVC) — 销售订单 OData V4 API 增强：在 2608 版本中，更多高级变式配置相关的字段与操作已通过销售订单 OData V4 API 对外开放。这使得在销售订单创建和处理过程中，系统集成场景得到进一步丰富，包括在订单模拟和处理期间对 AVC 配置数据的增强访问能力，为复杂的可配置产品场景提供了更完整的 API 支持。

生产订单 OData V4 API — 新增操作：在 2608 版本中，生产订单的 OData V4 API（API_PRODUCTIONORDER）新增了两项重要操作：

  • 合并操作 (Combine Action)：Combine 操作被添加到生产订单抬头节点，允许通过扩展将整批生产订单合并，大幅提升了离散制造场景的处理效率。
  • 重置可用性检查结果 (ResetAvailabilityCheckResult)：支持通过 API 重置生产订单的物料可用性检查结果，该操作同时适用于业务对象接口 (Business Object Interface) 和 OData V4 API。

采购申请变更 — 请及时关注：这是一个需要用户重点关注的变更。"处理采购申请 (Process Purchase Requisitions)" 应用已被标记为弃用 (Deprecated)，并将在未来版本中从 SAP Fiori 启动板上正式移除。SAP 建议用户尽快切换至其继任应用"处理采购申请（新版）"。API 服务 API_PURCHASEREQ_PROCESS 自 2402 开始已经标注启用，请尽快切换至后继 API 服务 API_PURCHASEREQUISITION_2 。与此同时，采购申请创建与更新服务的地址验证功能也得到了加强，请在集成开发中留意相关字段的校验逻辑变化。

关键用户扩展性增强

对于业务专家和关键用户而言，2608 版本在自定义字段和业务情景方面带来了重要提升：

仓库任务字段扩展性（Field Extensibility for Warehouse Tasks）— 重磅新功能：这是 2608 版本中可拓展性领域最受关注的新能力之一。企业往往需要在仓库任务处理过程中记录特定的业务信息，此前这一需求难以通过标准方式满足。从 2608 版本起，关键用户现在可以为仓库任务数据模型添加自定义字段，以存储企业特定的业务信息。具体而言：

  • 自定义字段可在 "处理仓库任务 (Process Warehouse Tasks)" 应用的界面中直接使用；
  • 同时，这些自定义字段也会在 仓库订单和仓库任务 API（OData 及 SOAP） 中得到暴露，确保字段数据能够在仓库流程和系统集成中完整流转；
  • 对于需要自定义逻辑的场景，可以通过 BAdI "内部仓库任务创建 (Internal Warehouse Task Creation)" 来实现进一步的业务逻辑扩展。

情景处理扩展性 (Situation Handling Extensibility) — 自定义电子邮件：在 2608 版本中，情景处理 (Situation Handling) 框架进一步扩展，支持为基于对象的情景 (Object-Based Situations) 自定义发送邮件内容。这意味着企业可以根据自身业务需求，为触发的业务情景配置个性化的通知邮件模板，使业务用户收到的提醒信息更加贴合实际工作场景，进一步提升了情景处理能力的灵活性。

中央采购新增 CDS 视图

在 2608 版本中，中央采购领域新增了多个已发布的 CDS 视图，为企业提供了更丰富的数据消费和扩展基础：

CDS 视图技术名称 说明

I_CNTRLSUPLRCONFBASIC中央供应商确认（抬头）
I_CNTRLSUPLRCONFITEMBASIC中央供应商确认（行项目）
I_CNTRLSUPLRCONFLINEBASIC中央供应商确认（明细行）
I_CEPUCOITMDISTRPART中央采购合同行项目分配合作伙伴

这些新发布的 CDS 视图可用于自定义分析查询、数据提取或进一步的 RAP 扩展开发场景，建议有中央采购集成需求的团队重点关注。

开发者扩展性增强 — 制造业合并生产订单

在开发者扩展性层面，制造业场景迎来了一项重要更新。在上一版本（2602）中，SAP 正式推出了合并生产订单功能，而在 2608 版本中，该功能的可扩展性接口得到了全面补齐：

  • 业务对象接口 (Business Object Interface)：Combine 操作已添加至生产订单抬头 (Production Order Header) 实体的扩展能力中，开发者现在可以将整批生产订单的合并逻辑纳入自定义扩展；
  • OData V4 API：ResetAvailabilityCheckResult 操作已添加至生产订单抬头 (Production Order Header) 实体，支持通过 API 重置物料可用性检查的结果。

这意味着，无论是通过业务对象接口还是通过 OData V4 API 进行集成开发，开发者都可以在遵循 Clean Core 原则的前提下，充分利用合并生产订单的新能力。

SAP Discovery Center 精选任务推荐 — 可拓展性专题

除了上述版本更新，SAP Discovery Center 持续提供结构化的实操任务，帮助合作伙伴和开发者将可拓展性能力落地为真实的业务解决方案。本期重点推荐以下任务：

以 SAP 合作伙伴身份，使用 SAP Build 和 CAP 构建旁挂式多租户应用 (Build a Side-by-Side Multi-Tenant Application with SAP Build and Cloud Application Programming Model (CAP) as an SAP Partner)

适用对象： SAP 合作伙伴（Partners Only）

当前挑战

作为 SAP 合作伙伴，您希望利用 SAP Cloud Application Programming Model（CAP）在 SAP BTP 上构建多租户应用，并将其与 SAP Cloud ERP 集成。然而，要设计出真正具备多租户能力、可作为 SaaS 产品商业化落地的解决方案，您需要在以下四个维度获得系统性的指引：架构设计、应用开发、运营维护 以及 商业模式。

任务目标

完成本任务后，您将能够：

  • 设计、构建并运营与 SAP Cloud ERP 无缝集成的多租户 SAP CAP 应用；
  • 构建可跨多个客户复用、具备规模化能力的 SaaS 解决方案；
  • 交付具备透明成本结构的合作伙伴级产品，并打通从初始开发、客户引导到长期运维的完整路径。

任务覆盖内容

本任务以一个合作伙伴参考应用作为可复用蓝图，端到端引导您完成以下旅程：

阶段 内容

测试与上线应用测试策略与客户 Onboarding 流程
运维管理多租户应用的生命周期运营与长期维护

多租户 (Multi-Tenancy) 是旁挂式扩展 (Side-by-Side Extensibility) 走向商业化 SaaS 产品的关键技术路径。如果您正计划基于 SAP BTP 构建面向多个终端客户的扩展解决方案，强烈建议参考本任务作为架构和开发起点。

entry.title: Workshop: Create AI Agents, scalable and SaaS Extensions for SAP Autonomous Suite
entry.content:
Many SAP partners already build extensions to address specific customer requirements. But turning a successful customer solution into a scalable product that can be deployed, operated, and supported across many customersrequires a different approach.

That is exactly what we want to explore in our upcoming hands-on partner workshop:

Create Scalable, Multitenant Extensions and AI Agents for SAP Autonomous Suite

The four-day, in-person workshop is designed for SAP partners who want to build scalable SaaS extensions and AI agents for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition using SAP Business Technology Platform (SAP BTP), SAP Build, the SAP Cloud Application Programming Model (CAP), AI services, and on-stack extensibility.

And importantly, the workshop is not only about how to build an extension. We will look at the complete journey from identifying a viable business opportunity to developing, publishing, operating, and supporting a partner solution at scale.

From Business Opportunity to Scalable Solution

Before investing in a new product, partners need to understand more than its technical feasibility.

During the workshop, we will therefore start with the business perspective: identifying market opportunities, understanding the SAP PartnerEdge – Build journey, estimating the total cost of ownership of a solution, and exploring how a partner product can ultimately be marketed and sold through SAP channels.

Participants will then work hands-on through the technical lifecycle of a scalable extension.

The objective is to help partners make fact-based decisions about what to build, how to build it, and what it takes to operate the solution successfully at scale.

What You Will Build and Explore

Day 1: Business Development and Market Opportunity

We start by looking at the business foundations of a scalable partner solution:

  • Business opportunity and solution overview
  • SAP PartnerEdge – Build program
  • Industry partner opportunity maps
  • TCO calculation for partner solutions
  • How to market and sell your solution via SAP Store

Days 1–3: Side-by-Side, Multitenant Extensions

The main hands-on part of the workshop focuses on building scalable SaaS extensions using SAP BTP and SAP Build.

Topics include:

  • Building multitenant CAP solutions
  • Deployment and provisioning of SaaS extensions
  • Integration with SAP Build Work Zone
  • Integration with SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition
  • SAP Document AI
  • Embedded AI using SAP AI Core

Participants will experience how the different components come together in a solution designed to serve multiple customers rather than a single implementation.

Day 3: Code-Based AI Agents

AI agents are increasingly becoming another way to extend and automate enterprise applications.

During a dedicated hands-on module, we will introduce:

  • Code-based AI agent development
  • Agentic approaches to extending business processes
  • How AI agents can interact with and automate scenarios around SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

This gives participants an opportunity to explore agentic development alongside more traditional extension patterns.

Day 4: On-Stack Extensibility

Not every extension needs to run side-by-side.

The final day therefore focuses on scalable extensions running directly on the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition stack, including:

  • Development of on-stack extensions
  • Scalable provisioning of on-stack extensions
  • Landscape Portal and the lifecycle of partner-built on-stack solutions

Together, these modules provide an overview of the different architectural options available to partners when designing a scalable extension.

Who Should Attend?

The workshop is primarily intended for SAP partners interested in creating reusable products, SaaS extensions, or AI-powered solutions for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

Because the hands-on exercises span both on-stack and side-by-side development, we recommend that partners participate with two people with complementary technical backgrounds:

  • One participant with ABAP experience
  • One participant with JavaScript/TypeScript experience and basic SAP BTP knowledge

Participants will work in pairs during the hands-on exercises and should bring their own devices.

Choose the Workshop Iteration That Works for You

Barcelona, Spain
October 5–8, 2026
Register for Barcelona

Bengaluru, India
October 26–29, 2026
Register for Bengaluru

Palo Alto, USA
November 16–19, 2026
Register for Palo Alto

Build for the Next Customer, Not Only the Current One

Customer-specific extensions will continue to be an important part of the SAP ecosystem. But for partners, there is an additional opportunity: taking expertise gained from individual implementations and turning it into repeatable intellectual property and scalable products.

That requires thinking about architecture, multitenancy, provisioning, lifecycle management, AI, operations, support, and the business model from the very beginning.

This workshop is designed to bring those pieces together.
