entry.title: SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition: Handling Missing Public APIs as a Partner — A Practical Guide
entry.content:
SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition: Handling Missing Public APIs as a Partner — A Practical Guide

Introduction

During SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition implementations and partner custom developments, partners occasionally encounter a scenario where a required API simply does not exist in the SAP Business Accelerator Hub. This gap can become a project blocker — particularly when third-party integrations or BTP side-by-side extensions depend on data objects that have no released API endpoint. During developer extensibiltiy on-stack customization of  SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition some of the required entities are not released for partner developement.

This blog post consolidates the recommended guidance for SAP partners on how to handle such situations. It covers the permanent resolution path via the SAP Customer Influence Programme (CIP), interim workaround options using Custom APIs, current known limitations, and the product improvements on SAP's roadmap.

Whether you are an implementation consultant, solution architect, partner enablement lead, or a partner developer, this guide provides the end-to-end picture.

The Scenario

You are mid-implementation of SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition or in the process of building partner add-on of SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. Your solution requires an API — either to expose data to a BTP extension or to support an on-stack integration — and it is nowhere to be found on the SAP Business Accelerator Hub.

Before raising alarms, it is important to understand the two distinct types of APIs involved:

  • Local APIs — CDS views, Business Object Interfaces used in On-Stack Extensionsibility using ABAP Cloud
  • Remote APIs — APIs consumed externally, typically by BTP side-by-side applications or third-party systems.

This distinction determines both the CIP campaign you should target and the workaround approach you should implement in the interim.

Permanent Solution: The SAP Customer Influence Programme (CIP)

The right long-term path for any missing API on SAP Business Accelerator Hub is a formal request through the SAP Customer Influence Programme. Here is the recommended step-by-step process:

Note: SAP Continuos Influence for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition (CIP) would be moved to new Aha platform in near future and after the migration the CIP sessions and request URLs will be redirected to the Aha! platform after go-live.

Step 1 — Verify the API is Genuinely Missing

Before submitting any request, search SAP Business Accelerator Hub thoroughly. Confirm the API does not exist in any form — sometimes a different naming convention or an OData version difference can cause confusion.

Note: Please try out Joule copilot in SAP Business Accelerator Hub , It helps you with all your queries on the content available.

Note: make sure to select SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition in the product list in the SAP Business Accelerator Hub

Step 2 — Determine the API Type

Classify the missing API as either a Local API (on-stack) or a Remote API (external/BTP-facing). This classification determines which CIP campaign to use.

Step 3 — Check for an Existing CIP Request

Search the relevant campaign before creating a new entry. If another partner has already submitted the same request:

  • Vote for it. Every vote increases priority visibility with the SAP product team.

If no matching request exists, submit a new one. for more details please refer to SAP Community - Continuous Influence for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

Step 4 — Submit via the Correct CIP Campaign

 

API TypeCIP Campaign LinkNotes
Remote APIsCampaign 1175For APIs consumed by external apps or BTP side-by-side extensions (Loosely Couple Extensions using SAP BTP)
Local APIsCampaign 2759For on-stack APIs consumed within the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public system (Tightly Couple Extension using ABAP Cloud)

SLA Note: SAP targets a response within 20 business days of submission. For priority cases, partners can escalate via a partner support ticket / partner escallation channel.

For more detaila about CIP please refer to details below:

  • SAP Continuous Influence for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition - Frequently Asked Questions
  • SAP Continuous Influence for SAP S/4HANA Cloud, Public Edition - Session List and Rules of Engagement 
  • Continuous Influence for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition | SAP Community

Temporary Workaround: Building a Custom API

While the CIP request works its way through the process, partners should not be left idle. Custom APIs provide a viable bridge. Two options are available as mentioned below.

Option 1: Custom CDS View Exposed as an External API

This is the preferred no-code/low-code approach that uses standard S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition on stack key user extensibility — no separate ABAP environment required.

Step 1 — Identify Released CDS Views Open the View Browser App in S/4HANA Cloud and locate released CDS views that can serve as the data source for your required API.

Step 2 — Create a Custom CDS View

  • Open the Custom CDS View App.
  • Select the relevant released CDS view(s) as the data source.
  • Add required fields, maintain field properties, and publish the Custom CDS View with the External API setting enabled.
  • Demo video - Creating Custom CDS Views as External APIs - SAP S/4HANA Cloud Extensibility

Step 3 — Expose via a Communication Scenario

  • Open the Custom Communication Scenario App and create a new Custom Communication Scenario.
  • Add the published Custom CDS View (External API) to the scenario and publish it.
  • Create a Communication Arrangement:
    • Assign the Custom Communication Scenario to the arrangement.
    • Create or maintain the Communication System and Communication User.
    • Activate the arrangement and copy the Service URL for testing.
  • Demo Video - Exposing Custom CDS Views as External APIs - SAP S/4HANA Cloud Extensibility

Step 4 — Test the Custom API Validate the endpoint using Postman or any API testing tool against the copied Service URL.

Note: The custom API's is a custom artifact created using above steps would allow Read-Only operation and would not support Create Update and Delete operations.

Option 2: RAP - Based API (ABAP Development)

For partners with access to an ABAP development environment — either BTP ABAP Environment or an S/4HANA Cloud development tenant — a RESTful ABAP Programming model (RAP) offers greater flexibility.

  1. Develop a RAP-based custom API using ABAP Development Tools (ADT).
  2. Release the custom API for ABAP Cloud consumption, making it a custom public API.
  3. Activate the released API via Communication Arrangements in the target tenant.

Custom API Delivery Approaches

Once a Custom API is built, partners need to decide how to deliver it — especially for multi-customer scenarios:

 

ApproachDescriptionBest Suited For
Multi Off (Multi-Customer Off-Stack)Package the custom API as part of an on-stack customization delivered via gCTS (Git-enabled Change and Transport System)Partners delivering solutions to few customers.
Scalable (Cross-Stack Extension)Combine an on-stack add-on (custom API on S/4HANA) with a side-by-side BTP extension that consumes the API.Packaged ABAP Cloud AddOn delivered  to customer via SAP Store using Landscape Portal.

Current Known Facts:

It would be remiss not to highlight the gaps that currently constrain these workarounds:

  1. Read-Only Operations Only: Custom APIs currently support only READ (GET) operations. Create, Update, and Delete (CUD) operations are not supported. This works as designed since CDS views are released for Readonly operation.

  2. Unreleased CDS Views: Not all CDS views have been released for custom use. This directly blocks Option 1 for certain data objects, forcing partners toward the more complex RAP-based approach or leaving them temporarily without a viable workaround. in such cases please follow CIP request approach.

  3. On-Stack Dependency for Multi-Tenant SaaS: Partners building multi-tenant SaaS applications that consume Custom APIs are required to deliver an on-stack extension component — adding architectural complexity and incremental cost to their delivery model. This works as designed since its a Cross Stack custom solution.

Summary and Recommended Actions

Here is a consolidated view of what partners should do today:

 

Area Recommended Action
CIP SubmissionCheck CIP campaigns 1175 (Remote) and 2759 (Local) — vote on existing requests or submit new ones.
Custom APIsUse Custom CDS Views (Option 1) or RAP wrappers (Option 2) as an interim workaround while CIP requests are processed.
CUD OperationsFlag any use cases requiring Create/Update/Delete operations — escalate via partner support if this is a project blocker.
CDS View GapsIf Option 1 is blocked due to an unreleased CDS view, submit via CIP Campaign 2759 and request fast-track review.
Multi-Tenant ArchitectureEngage with SAP Architecture / Partner Reference Applications (PRA) teams for guidance on on-stack add-on and cross-stack delivery models.

Closing Thoughts

Missing Public APIs need not be a dead-end for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition implementations. The path forward is clear: use the SAP Customer Influence Programme as the permanent vehicle for getting APIs officially released, and leverage Custom APIs as a structured, supported interim solution.

The combination of partner advocacy through CIP voting, tactical Custom API development, and SAP's roadmap commitments around CRUD support and CDS view releases should collectively close the gap — both today and over the coming release cycles.

If you have encountered similar challenges in your own S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition projects, consider voting on the relevant CIP campaigns and sharing your use case — your input directly shapes the product roadmap.

Key Reference Links

  • Overview | SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition | SAP Business Accelerator Hub
  • Remote APIs — CIP Campaign: https://influence.sap.com/sap/ino/#/campaign/1175
  • Local APIs — CIP Campaign : https://influence.sap.com/sap/ino/#/campaign/2759
  • SAP Community Blog Post - New Guided Missions for SAP Partners: Build Once. Scale to Many
  • Build Solutions for SAP Cloud ERP with confidence - SAP Community

This blog post is based on guidance current as of 2026. The CRUD operation gap and unreleased CDS view limitations are actively tracked as product improvement items.

entry.title: Sales Order Approval for High Manual Discounts Using Flexible Workflow in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public
entry.content:
Sales Order Approval for High Manual Discounts Using Flexible Workflow in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

Introduction

During a recent SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition implementation, I came across a requirement where the business wanted additional control over manual discounts in sales orders.

The sales team was authorized to maintain manual discount conditions during sales order creation, which is a standard business practice. But, the CRO, CFO & CIO wanted visibility and approval control whenever the discount crossed a certain percentage. Their concern  about ensuring that unusually high discounts were reviewed before the sales order continued further in the process.

To address this requirement, I used SAP Flexible Workflow together with the standard BAdI SD_APM_SET_APPROVAL_REASON to automatically trigger an approval process whenever a manual discount exceeded 10%.

In this blog, I will walk through the configuration and custom logic I used to achieve this requirement in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

Business Justification

We can implement Access Control for Pricing Elements to restrict who can create, modify, or apply manual discounts. However, authorization control alone does not provide sufficient oversight over the actual discount values being granted to customers.

For example, a sales representative may be authorized to apply manual discounts as part of the sales process. While this authorization ensures that only designated users can maintain pricing conditions, it does not prevent excessive discounts that could negatively impact business profitability.

To address this challenge, organizations often introduce an approval process for discounts that exceed a predefined threshold. This enables management to review exceptional pricing decisions while allowing day-to-day sales activities to continue without unnecessary intervention.

Business Requirement

The requirement was straightforward:

  • Sales users should continue to maintain manual discounts in sales orders.
  • Discounts up to 10% should not require any approval.
  • If a manual discount exceeds 10%, the sales order should be automatically sent for approval.
  • The order should remain pending until an approver reviews and approves it.
  • Approvers should receive the request in My Inbox and be able to approve, reject, or send it back for rework.

The objective was to introduce approval control only for exceptional discount scenarios while keeping the standard sales process simple and efficient for normal transactions.

Prerequisites

Before proceeding with the configuration, ensure that the following prerequisites are met:

  1. Access to SAP Central Business Configuration (CBC) to maintain the required configuration settings.

  2. Approval Reason Configuration for Sales Documents must be completed and available for use within the approval process.

  3. Custom Logic App Access to implement the business logic required for determining approval conditions based on manual discount values.

  4. Access to the Manage Teams and Responsibilities App to define approvers and maintain responsibility assignments.

  5. Access to the Manage Workflows for Sales Orders App to create and configure the approval workflow.

  6. Access to My Inbox for workflow approvers to review, approve, or reject sales order approval requests.

For role and business or technical catalogue info, please visit FIORI app library - https://fioriappslibrary.hana.ondemand.com/sap/fix/externalViewer/#/home 

Key Configuration Steps 

Pricing Configuration Requirements

For this blog, the custom discount condition type ZMAN is used to represent the manual discount.

To enable the approval workflow to evaluate the discount percentage, Subtotal 1 is assigned to condition type ZMAN within the pricing procedure. This allows the system to capture the manual discount value in a dedicated subtotal field, which can then be read through custom logic and used to determine whether the approval workflow should be triggered.

The configuration is illustrated below:

  • Condition Type: ZMAN
  • Purpose: Manual Discount
  • Pricing Procedure: Assigned as per customer pricing procedure
  • Subtotal: 1

By storing the manual discount in Subtotal 1, the custom workflow logic can retrieve the discount percentage and compare it against the defined approval threshold (10% in this example). If the discount exceeds the threshold, the sales order is routed for approval; otherwise, it proceeds through the standard order processing flow.

This setup ensures that the approval decision is based on the actual manual discount applied in the sales order.

  1. Configure ZMAN pricing condition type for manual discount with Subtotal 1 (in pricing procedure). 


2. Define and assign approval reason ZMAN in CBC. 

In this step, navigate to SAP Central Business Configuration (CBC) and define an approval reason that will later be used in the custom logic to trigger the approval workflow.

Define Approval Request Reason

First, we have to create a new approval request reason.

For this example, the following approval reason is created:

Assign Approval Request Reason

Next, we have to assign the approval reason to the relevant sales document category.

Here, document category "C" represents a Sales Order. The custom logic will evaluate the manual discount maintained using condition type ZMAN and, when the defined threshold is exceeded, automatically set the approval request reason. This approval request reason is then used by the Flexible Workflow to trigger the approval process.

3. Maintain Approval Team and Responsibilities

In this step, configure the approval team that will be responsible for reviewing and approving sales orders requiring approval.

Navigate to the Manage Teams and Responsibilities app and click Create.

Create Team

Maintain the following details:

  • Team Name: Enter a team name
  • Global Team ID: This value is automatically derived from the team name.
  • Team Type: Select SALES.

Add Team Members

Next, navigate to the Team Members tab and add the users who will participate in the approval process.

For each team member, maintain the appropriate function or role, such as:

  • Approver 1
  • Approver 2

Additional approvers can be added based on the organization's approval hierarchy and business requirements.

Purpose of the Team Configuration

The approval team defined in this step will be used by the Flexible Workflow to determine the approvers responsible for reviewing sales orders that exceed the defined manual discount threshold. When a sales order triggers the workflow, the approval request is routed to the relevant team members, who can review and approve or reject the request directly from My Inbox.

4. Configure the Sales Order Approval Workflow

In this step, use the Manage Workflows for Sales Orders app to configure the workflow conditions, approval steps, and rework actions required for the sales order approval process.

Navigate to the Manage Workflows for Sales Orders app and select Sales Orders from the workflow scenario drop-down list. After selecting the scenario, click Create to create a new workflow.

Maintain General Information

Enter the workflow details, such as:

  • Workflow Name
  • Description
  • Validity Period (if applicable)
  • Workflow Order

The workflow order determines the sequence in which workflows are evaluated if multiple workflows exist for the same business object.

Define Workflow Start Conditions

Next, configure the start conditions that determine when the workflow should be triggered.

For this scenario, the workflow should be triggered when the approval request reason ZMAN is set by the custom logic for sales orders containing a manual discount greater than 10%.

Configure Approval Step

Add a workflow step and select Approval as the step type.

In the recipient determination section, select the team that was created in the Manage Teams and Responsibilities app. This ensures that the approval request is routed to the designated sales approvers.

Configure Rework Step

To allow users to modify and resubmit rejected sales orders, configure a Rework step.

When an approver rejects the workflow, the sales order is returned to the initiator for correction and resubmission. The user can then adjust the discount value or other relevant details and submit the sales order for approval again.

Activate the Workflow

After completing the configuration, save and activate the workflow.

Once activated, sales orders containing a manual discount greater than 10% will automatically trigger the approval process and be routed to the designated approvers for review.


5.Implement Custom Logic Using the Approval Reason BAdI

In this step, implement the SAP standard Business Add-In (BAdI) SD_APM_SET_APPROVAL_REASON using the Custom Logic app.

Navigation

Open the Custom Logic app and create a new implementation for the following enhancement:

Logic I have used -

" Loop through items to check for the manual discount (ZMAN)

LOOP AT salesdocumentitem INTO DATA(ls_item).

" Subtotal 1 holds the value of your manual discount (ZMAN)
IF abs( ls_item-subtotal1amount ) > 10.

" Set the Approval Reason code for manual discount
salesdocapprovalreason = 'ZMAN'.

" Exit the loop once the reason is set
EXIT.
ENDIF.

ENDLOOP.

Custom Logic Explanation

The custom logic loops through all sales order items and reads the value stored in Subtotal 1, which contains the manual discount percentage from condition type ZMAN.

If the manual discount exceeds 10%, the system automatically sets the Approval Request Reason to ZMAN and exits the loop. Once the approval reason is assigned, the Flexible Workflow identifies the sales order as requiring approval and triggers the approval process.

If the discount is 10% or less, no approval reason is assigned, and the sales order continues through the standard processing flow without triggering the workflow.

The logic reads Subtotal 1. If the discount is greater than 10%, Approval Reason ZMAN is assigned and the workflow starts. 

Testing the Approval Workflow

To validate the configuration, create a sales order and apply a manual discount greater than the defined approval threshold of 10% using condition type ZMAN.

In this example, a manual discount of 11% is applied through condition type ZMAN and the sales order is saved.

When the document is saved, the custom logic reads the discount value stored in Subtotal 1. Since the discount exceeds the configured threshold, the system automatically assigns the approval request reason ZMAN and triggers the sales order approval workflow.

As a result, an approval task is generated and routed to the designated approver(s) configured in the Manage Teams and Responsibilities app.

Expected Result

  • Sales Order is created with 11% manual discount.
  • Approval Request Reason ZMAN is automatically assigned.
  • Workflow is triggered successfully.
  • Approval work item is sent to the approver's My Inbox.
  • The sales order remains pending until the approval decision is completed.

This confirms that the approval workflow is correctly evaluating the manual discount and triggering the approval process whenever the configured threshold is exceeded.

Conclusion

In this blog, I demonstrated how to configure a Sales Order Approval Workflow for high manual discounts in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. By combining Flexible Workflow, Teams and Responsibilities, and the standard BAdI SD_APM_SET_APPROVAL_REASON, sales orders with a manual discount greater than 10% can be automatically routed for approval while preventing further processing until the approval is completed.

entry.title: The SAP Extended Warehouse Management FAQ Series: Delivery interface extensibility for Public Cloud
entry.content:
In complex warehouse landscapes, customers often extend SAP delivery objects with customer-specific fields to capture business-critical information beyond standard SAP content. In a setup where SAP Extended Warehouse Management (EWM) runs in a decentralized SAP S/4HANA system integrated to an ERP system in the SAP Public Cloud, transmitting these extended field values reliably to EWM becomes a key integration requirement.

With this blog post, we would like to address some of the most frequently asked questions around delivery object extensibility in decentralized EWM environments integrated to an ERP Public Cloud system.

 

 

 What is the scenario we are addressing?

You are running EWM in a decentralized SAP S/4HANA (Private Edition) system, integrated to an ERP system in the SAP Public Cloud. You have extended your ERP delivery object with customer-specific fields using the standard Public Cloud extensibility app — and now you want to ensure that the values of those fields are transmitted to the corresponding customer fields of your EWM delivery object in the decentralized system.

In the ERP Public Cloud system, all delivery interfaces are extended automatically when you create customer fields via the extension app. The transfer of delivery data between the systems is executed via Function Module `/SCWM/*_DLV_SAVEREPLICA` over QRFC. The extended field values are packed into the `extension2` table as name-value pairs in a field of type `CHAR 255`.

Why are my customer field values not visible in SMQ2 or the debugger?

This is a known behavior. Depending on the data type of your customer field, the value may not be immediately visible in transaction SMQ2 or in the standard debugger view. The reason is that the value can be located at the right-hand end of the CHAR 255 string, beyond the visible portion of the standard display.

To verify the value is actually present, download the queue entry to a file or scroll to the very end of the 255-character string in the debugger — the value will be visible there.

How do I map the customer field values from the ERP delivery to the EWM delivery?

In your decentralized EWM S/4HANA system, you need to implement the relevant BAdIs of the enhancement spot `/SCWM/ES_ERP_MAPIN`. For inbound and outbound delivery scenarios, you must implement the following two BAdIs respectively:

  • /SCWM/EX_ERP_MAPIN_ID_SAVEREPL — for inbound delivery mapping
  • /SCWM/EX_ERP_MAPIN_OD_SAVEREPL — for outbound delivery mapping

Learn more about extensibility incl. example coding via SAP Note 3796221 - Integration of EWM in S/4 HANA decentral to ERO in the Public Cloud: Delivery Object Extensibility.

What are the key implementation considerations?

When implementing the BAdI mapping logic, keep the following points in mind:

  • CHAR 255 type conversion: The `value` field in `it_bapi_extension2` is always of type `CHAR 255`. You must explicitly convert this value to the actual data type of your target EWM delivery customer field. For numeric, date, or other non-character fields, ensure correct type handling to avoid data loss or runtime errors.
  • Header vs. Item fields: Handle header fields and item fields separately. Item-level fields require resolving the item number via `t_keymap_item` before matching entries in `bapi_extension2`.
  • Parameterization: The `param` field differentiates between header entries (`SAP_EXTEND_HEAD`) and item entries (`SAP_EXTEND_ITEM`). Ensure your filter conditions are precise.
  • Naming alignment: The field name in the ERP extension (`ZZ_FIELDNAME_HEADER_ERP`) does not need to match the EWM field name (`ZZ_FIELDNAME_HEADER_EWM`), but the mapping must be explicitly defined in your BAdI implementation.
  • Non-compilable example: The example code above will not compile as-is. Replace all placeholder field names and structure references with your actual customer field definitions.

Where can I find more information?

For further details and reference information, please consult:

  • SAP Note 3796221 — Integration of EWM in S/4HANA Decentral to ERP in the Public Cloud: Delivery Object Extensibility (released 26.08.2026)
  • SAP Help Portal — Enhancement Spot `/SCWM/ES_ERP_MAPIN` and available BAdIs for delivery processing
  • SAP Blogs - The SAP Extended Warehouse Management FAQ Series: SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud Integration

We hope this FAQ helps you successfully implement customer field extensibility in your decentralized EWM delivery integration. Stay tuned for further posts in the SAP EWM FAQ Series covering additional integration and extensibility topics.

entry.title: Additional Quantity Reporting in Margin Analysis Using a Quantity Conversion Extension
entry.content:
The Problem

In many businesses, the same product is sold in different units of measure depending on the customer, the order type, or the packaging: one customer orders in individual Bottles (BT), another in Cartons (CAR), and yet another in full Pallets (PAL). This is common practice within a single sales organization and has no impact on the sales or logistics process. However, it creates a reporting challenge in Margin Analysis.

The apps of the Market Segments family — such as Profitability — Market Segments — display quantity measures (Valuation Quantity, Act Valuation Qty, Act Reference Qty, Act Qty in Base Unit) in whichever unit of measure was used on the originating billing document. Without a conversion to a unified base unit, it is impossible to aggregate or compare sold volumes across line items, customers, or periods. Customers want to see their contribution margin not only per sales unit — which differs by packaging — but also per base unit, enabling a true like-for-like comparison.

Operating across multiple sales organizations that invoice in different units adds a further dimension to the same challenge, but the core problem is already present within a single sales organization.

You may notice that apps in the Sales Volumes family do not have this problem: they correctly convert quantities to a unified base unit. This is not a bug in either app family — it reflects a fundamental difference in where each reads its data.

 

Market Segments Apps

Sales Volumes Apps

Data source

Universal Journal (ACDOCA) — CO document items

Billing document tables (VBRP)

UoM at posting time

Billing/sales UoM stored as-is in the CO document

Full SD document chain with material master conversion available

Result

Shows original sales unit (e.g., 30 CAR)

Can convert to base unit (e.g., 300 BT)

 

When a billing document is posted, the SD-to-CO transfer writes the billing quantity into the CO document item and from there into ACDOCA in the billing UoM, without converting to the material's base unit. The Quantity Conversion Extension described in this blog closes this gap by populating additional quantity fields at posting time.

Section 1: Prerequisites — Product Master Data Setup

To demonstrate the Quantity Conversion Extension, three products representing the same physical item — water — are created, each sold in a different packaging unit. All three products are set up in the Manage Product Master Data app in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

 

Figure 1: Overview of the three products RR01, RR02, RR03 in Manage Product Master Data

All three products are of type Trading Goods (HAWA) and share the same base unit: Bottle (BT). This is a critical design choice — the base unit acts as the common denominator to which all alternative units are converted.

Product RR01 — Water - Bottle

RR01 has only one unit of measure defined: Bottle (BT), with a self-referencing conversion of 1 BT = 1 BT. This is the simplest case — the product is sold in its base unit, so no conversion is needed.

Figure 2: RR01 — Units of Measure, base unit Bottle (BT) only

Product RR02 — Water - Carton

RR02 has two units of measure: Bottle (BT) as the base unit, and Carton (CAR) as an alternative sales unit with the conversion factor 1 CAR = 10 BT. This conversion factor, defined on the General Information tab under Units of Measure, tells the system how many bottles are contained in one carton.

Figure 3: RR02 — Units of Measure showing 1 CAR = 10 BT

On the Distribution Chains tab, the Sales Unit for Sales Organization 1010 / Direct Sales (10) is set to Carton (CAR). This means sales orders for RR02 default to CAR as the invoicing unit.

Figure 4: RR02 — Distribution Chains showing Sales Unit = CAR

Product RR03 — Water - Pallet

RR03 follows the same pattern with a larger packaging unit: Bottle (BT) as the base unit, and Pallet (PAL) with the conversion factor 1 PAL = 180 BT. One pallet contains 180 bottles (equivalent to 18 cartons of 10 bottles each).

Figure 5: RR03 — Units of Measure showing 1 PAL = 180 BT

Accordingly, the Sales Unit for this product is set to Pallet (PAL) in the Distribution Chains.

Figure 6: RR03 — Distribution Chains showing Sales Unit = PAL

Why This Setup Matters

The conversion factors defined in the product master are the foundation of the entire Quantity Conversion Extension. Without them, there is no basis for converting quantities at any point in the process. The table below shows the full picture — base unit, sales unit, and the conversion factor for each product:

Product ID

Description

Base Unit

Sales Unit of Measure

Conversion Factor

RR01

Water - Bottle

Bottle (BT)

Bottle (BT)

1 BT = 1 BT

RR02

Water - Carton

Bottle (BT)

Carton (CAR)

1 CAR = 10 BT

RR03

Water - Pallet

Bottle (BT)

Pallet (PAL)

1 PAL = 180 BT

Note: Every product sold in a non-base unit must have its alternative UoM conversion defined on the product master before any sales orders or billing documents are created. Missing conversions will cause the extension to fall back to the original sales unit quantity.

Section 3: Creating the BAdI Implementation in the Custom Logic App

The Quantity Conversion Extension is created entirely through the Custom Logic app — no external development tools or transport requests are required. This app is SAP's entry point for BAdI-based extensibility in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, fully aligned with the Clean Core principle.

Step 1 — Find the Extension Point

Open the Custom Logic app and choose New Implementation. In the Extension Point search field, enter FIN_CODOC_ITEM_QUANTITY and press Search.

Figure 8: Searching for BAdI FIN_CODOC_ITEM_QUANTITY in the Custom Logic app

The system returns exactly one result:

Description

ID

Controlling Document Line Item Additional Quantities

FIN_CODOC_ITEM_QUANTITY

 

This BAdI is called every time a Controlling document line item is created — for example, when a billing document is transferred to Margin Analysis. The View Documentation link provides the full interface specification directly in the system. Select the entry and proceed to Step 2.

Step 2 — Implementation Attributes

In the Implementation Attributes section, BAdI filters can optionally be defined to restrict when the implementation is executed. In this scenario, no filters are needed — the extension applies to all relevant postings, so the Filters table is left empty.

Step 3 — Implementation ID

Figure 9: Implementation Attributes and Implementation ID

Field

Value

Implementation Description

Additional Product Quantities

Implementation ID

YY1_ADDITIONALPRODUCTQUANTITIE

 

The prefix YY1_ is the customer namespace for custom implementations in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, ensuring clean separation from SAP standard objects. Once the details are entered, click Review to validate, then Create to generate the implementation shell.

Section 4: Implementing the Code in the Custom Logic Editor

After clicking Create, the system opens the Custom Logic code editor. The implementation is developed on the Develop tab. The right-hand panel shows all available BAdI parameters — two importing structures are key:

Structure

Description

Key Fields Used

CODOCHEADER

CO Document Header

REFERENCEDOCUMENTTYPE (VBRK = Billing, MKPF = Material Doc)

CODOCITEM

CO Document Line Item

MATERIAL, TOTALQUANTITY, UNITUOM, PLANT, SALESORGANIZATION

 

The output variables ADDITIONALQUANTITY1, ADDITIONALQUANTITY1UNIT, ADDITIONALQUANTITY2, and ADDITIONALQUANTITY2UNIT are writable — the code writes the calculated values into them before the CO document item is persisted to ACDOCA.

 

Figure 10: Custom Logic editor — published code and BAdI parameter panel

The Code

IF codocitem-material IS NOT INITIAL AND

   ( codocheader-referencedocumenttype = 'MKPF' OR

     codocheader-referencedocumenttype = 'VBRK' ).

 

  IF codocitem-unituom IS NOT INITIAL.

 

    "AdditionalQuantity1: Convert Sales UoM to base unit for billing docs.

    "For material documents the quantity is already in base unit.

    IF codocheader-referencedocumenttype = 'VBRK'.

      SELECT SINGLE

          GrossWeight,

          WeightUnit,

          QuantityNumerator,

          QuantityDenominator,

          BaseUnit

        FROM I_ProductUnitsOfMeasure

        WHERE Product         = @codocitem-material

          AND AlternativeUnit = @codocitem-unituom

       INTO @DATA(ls_uom).

      IF sy-subrc = 0.

        additionalquantity1unit = ls_uom-baseunit.

        additionalquantity1     = codocitem-totalquantity

                                  * ls_uom-quantitynumerator

                                  / ls_uom-quantitydenominator.

      ELSE.

        additionalquantity1unit = codocitem-unituom.

        additionalquantity1     = codocitem-totalquantity.

      ENDIF.

    ELSE.

      "MKPF: quantity already in base unit

      additionalquantity1unit = codocitem-unituom.

      additionalquantity1     = codocitem-totalquantity.

    ENDIF.

 

    "AdditionalQuantity2: Gross weight of the posted quantity

    "Step 1: Try to read weight directly for the UoM of the posting

    IF ls_uom IS INITIAL.

      SELECT SINGLE

          GrossWeight,

          WeightUnit,

          QuantityNumerator,

          QuantityDenominator,

          BaseUnit

        FROM I_ProductUnitsOfMeasure

        WHERE Product         = @codocitem-material

          AND AlternativeUnit = @codocitem-unituom

       INTO @LS_uom.

    ENDIF.

 

    IF sy-subrc = 0 AND ls_uom-GrossWeight IS NOT INITIAL.

      "Weight is maintained per UoM — multiply directly

      additionalquantity2     = codocitem-totalquantity * ls_uom-GrossWeight.

      additionalquantity2unit = ls_uom-WeightUnit.

      RETURN.

    ENDIF.

 

    "Step 2: Fall back to base-unit weight from I_Product

    SELECT SINGLE

        GrossWeight,

        WeightUnit,

        BaseUnit

      FROM I_Product

      WHERE Product = @codocitem-material

      INTO @DATA(ls_product).

 

    IF sy-subrc = 0 AND ls_product-GrossWeight IS NOT INITIAL.

      "Use base-unit quantity (additionalquantity1) x weight per base unit

      additionalquantity2     = additionalquantity1 * ls_product-GrossWeight.

      additionalquantity2unit = ls_product-weightunit.

    ELSE.

      "No weight data available

      additionalquantity2 = 0.

      CLEAR additionalquantity2unit.

    ENDIF.

 

  ENDIF.

ENDIF.

Code Walkthrough

Entry Condition

The BAdI is called for every CO document item. The code only acts when a material is present on the line item and the posting originates from a billing document (VBRK) or a material document / goods issue (MKPF). All other document types — manual journal entries, allocations — are skipped.

Additional Quantity 1 — Base Unit Quantity

The behavior of Additional Quantity 1 differs depending on the source document type.

For billing documents (VBRK), the CO document item carries the quantity in the sales unit of measure — the unit the customer was invoiced in (e.g., CAR or PAL). The system does not automatically convert this to the base unit when writing to ACDOCA. The extension therefore performs this conversion explicitly by reading the product's UoM conversion factors from the released CDS view I_ProductUnitsOfMeasure. The result is the quantity expressed in the product's base unit — for example, 30 CAR becomes 300 BT. If no conversion record exists, the original sales unit quantity is used as a safe fallback.

For material documents (MKPF) — such as goods issues — SAP already converts the quantity to the base unit automatically during posting. No additional conversion is needed, so the code simply passes the existing quantity and unit through to Additional Quantity 1 unchanged.

Additional Quantity 2 — Product Mass

For all document types (both VBRK and MKPF), Additional Quantity 2 is populated with the gross weight of the posted quantity. This enables weight-based analysis in the Market Segments apps regardless of whether the posting originated from a billing or a goods movement.

The weight is determined in two steps: first by checking whether a gross weight is maintained directly on the alternative unit of measure in I_ProductUnitsOfMeasure; if not, by falling back to the base-unit weight from I_Product and multiplying it by the base-unit quantity already calculated in Additional Quantity 1.

Key Design Decisions

Decision

Rationale

Only VBRK and MKPF

Avoids unintended side effects on other CO posting types

I_ProductUnitsOfMeasure (CDS view)

Released SAP API — clean core compliant

Fallback to original UoM if no conversion found

Prevents data loss for products without alternative UoM definitions

Two-step weight logic

Supports both detailed per-UoM weight maintenance and simpler base-unit weight setups

 

Publishing the Implementation

Once the code is saved, it is in draft status and not yet active. To activate the extension, click Publish in the Custom Logic editor. After publishing, the editor confirms the activation with the publisher name and timestamp. From this point on, every new CO document item created from a billing document or material document will be processed by the BAdI.

Note: Only published implementations are active. If you later edit the code, the changes remain in draft until you publish again. The previously published version continues to run in the meantime.

Section 5: Creating the Sales Order

With the product master data configured and the Quantity Conversion Extension published, we use the Manage Sales Orders app to create Sales Order 14487 — a Standard Order (OR) with three line items, one for each of the three water products.

Section 7: Delivery, Billing, and the Complete Process Flow

With the sales order in place, we process the outbound delivery and create the billing document. The full document chain can be traced on the Process Flow tab of Sales Order 14487.

Posting to Ledger 0L

With the billing document completed, revenue and COGS are now posted in Ledger 0L — the leading operational ledger. Two CO document items are created:

  • From the billing document (VBRK): The Quantity Conversion Extension converts billing quantities from their sales units to the base unit BT and writes the result into Additional Quantity 1. Additional Quantity 2 is populated with the gross weight.

From the delivery / goods issue (MKPF): SAP already converts goods issue quantities to the base unit automatically. The extension passes the quantity through unchanged.

We return to the Product Profitability Review Booklet. The layout now shows both Ledger 0E and Ledger 0L side by side as column dimensions, giving a clear picture of how the predictive postings have been replaced by the actual postings.

Once the billing document was created and posted to Ledger 0L, the system automatically reversed the predicted postings in Ledger 0E. Conclusion and Summary

This blog has demonstrated how the Quantity Conversion Extension based on BAdI FIN_CODOC_ITEM_QUANTITY addresses a real reporting challenge in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition: the inability of the Market Segments app family to display quantities in a unified unit of measure when different subsidiaries or sales channels invoice in different sales units.

The solution is built entirely on SAP's supported extensibility framework — no modifications, no custom tables, no transport requests outside the Clean Core model. The steps covered end-to-end are:

  1. Product Master Data — Define alternative units of measure with conversion factors (e.g., 1 CAR = 10 BT, 1 PAL = 180 BT) and assign the correct sales unit per distribution chain.
  2. Configuration (SSCUI 102406) — Activate Additional Quantity fields in Profitability Analysis with the appropriate physical dimensions (No dimensions for countable units, Mass for weight).
  3. Custom Logic App — Create a BAdI implementation for FIN_CODOC_ITEM_QUANTITY (Controlling Document Line Item Additional Quantities) with no filters required.

  5. Publish — Activate the implementation in the Custom Logic app.

 

The result is verified in the Product Profitability Review Booklet, where Billed Additional Quantity 1 shows all products in the unified base unit, and the calculated measure CM I per Base Unit delivers a comparable margin metric across products — regardless of the invoicing unit. The extension also works seamlessly with Predictive Accounting (Ledger 0E), with predicted postings correctly cleared and replaced by actual Ledger 0L postings once billing is complete.

entry.title: How to Create an RAP Based Custom UI5 App and Deploy it to SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud
entry.content:
Image/data in this blog is from SAP internal systems, sample data, or demo systems. Any resemblance to real data is purely coincidental.

Do you want to build a custom SAPUI5/Fiori application on SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition using the ABAP RESTful Application Programming Model (RAP) and make it available as a tile in the SAP Fiori Launchpad?

This blog walks you through the complete end-to-end process — from creating the RAP-based OData service in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, developing a Fiori Elements List Report application in SAP Business Application Studio (BAS), deploying the application to SAP S/4HANA Cloud, and finally configuring the required IAM objects to make the application available as a tile in the Fiori Launchpad.

The complete flow covered in this blog is:

RAP Backend → OData Service → Fiori Elements Application → Deployment → IAM Configuration → Business Role → Fiori Launchpad

Overview: SAP Fiori Element Applications in the ABAP Environment

The above diagram illustrates that a UI developer implements the SAP Fiori application against the OData service and defines the tile as part of the application. Once this is done, the developer deploys the SAP Fiori application to the SAPUI5 ABAP repository in the development tenant.

An administrator provides access to the OData service and the tile via a business role.

A business user that is assigned to the business role can access the tile from SAP Fiori launchpad and launch the application.

Generating and Deploying Your Application

Before generating and deploying the application, ensure that the following prerequisites are met:

​Prerequisites

  • Need to create development package in ABAP Development Tools for Eclipse. See Creating ABAP Packages.
  • Need to expose a RAP business service as an OData service. See Using Service Binding Editor for OData V2 Service.
  • Business catalog SAP_A4C_BC_DEV_UID_PC is assigned to your user, which allows you to discover available OData services and deploy your application.
  • Business catalog SAP_CORE_BC_EXT_TST is assigned to your user, which allows you to preview your application. See Generate Deployment Configuration ABAP.
  • You have an open transport request.

With the prerequisites in place, let's proceed step by step to create and deploy a RAP-based custom SAPUI5 application in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

Step 1: Create RAP business service as an OData service using ADT.

Flow : Development Package -> Data Definition -> Service Definition -> Service Binding (RAP business service as an OData service)

  1. Open ADT and connect to development tenant
  2. Create Development package
  3. Create Data Definition
  4. Create Service Definition -> Reference Object ->Click on Browse -> Search and Select Standard data source (Example: I_PURCHASEORDERAPI01)
  5. Create Service Binding

     

Step 2: Generating and Deploying RAP Based Custom UI5 Application.

  1. Open Business Application Studio via BTP Cockpit 
  2. BAS is accessed through the SAP BTP Cockpit — not through the S/4HANA Fiori Launchpad. Open BTP Cockpit → Subaccount → Instances and Subscriptions.
  3. Launch the SAP Business Application Studio and Create a New Dev Space
  4. Select SAP Fiori -> Create Dev Space -> Open the Dev Space
  5. Create Project from Template
  6. Select SAP Fiori Generator -> List Report Page -> Select the System as "Development tenant -> Service as "Service Binding created using the ADT"
  7. Select Entity set and Table type as "Responsive".
  8. Fill all the Project Attributes.
  9. Define the "Deployment Configuration" ->Create the SAPUI5 ABAP Repository (name should have prefix as Z*)
  10. Define the Fiori Launchpad Configuration.
  11. Click on Finish.
  12. Click on Preview Application and test the application.
  13. Click on Deploy.
  14. Check the Terminal message shown as "Deployment Successful" .

Step 3: Testing RAP-Based Application in S/4HANA Public Cloud

Deployed a RAP-based application in the SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud system, However, while testing the application, I encountered an authorization issue when trying to consume the service in the SAP Fiori app.

How to handle Authorization Issues During UI Preview

  1. Create IAM App using ADT

     

  2. Check the BSP Library and Fiori User Interface (Which is auto generated once the application deployed successfully)
  3. Assign the "Fiori Launchpad App Descr Item ID" to IAM App.
  4. Publish Locally.
  5. Create Business Catalog and assign the IAM App.
  6. Publish Locally.
  7. Launch the Fiori Launchpad (S/4HANA Public Cloud Development System).
  8. Create the Business Role using the "Maintain Business Role" App.
  9. Assign the Business catalog and Business user to a Business Role.
  10. Try accessing the RAP Based Custom UI5 Application.

Summary:

In this blog, we explored the complete end-to-end process of building and deploying a RAP-based custom SAPUI5/Fiori application in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

Starting with the creation of a RAP business service in ABAP Development Tools (ADT), we exposed the business data as an OData service and consumed it in a Fiori Elements List Report application generated in SAP Business Application Studio (BAS). We then deployed the application to the SAPUI5 ABAP Repository in the SAP S/4HANA Cloud development tenant and verified the successful deployment.

We also covered the authorization and launchpad integration aspects by creating the required IAM App and Business Catalog, assigning them to a Business Role, and making the application available as a tile in the SAP Fiori Launchpad. This final step ensures that business users can securely access the application through role-based authorizations.

Conclusion:

The combination of the ABAP RESTful Application Programming Model (RAP), SAP Fiori Elements, and SAP Business Application Studio provides a streamlined approach for developing enterprise applications on SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

By following the steps outlined in this blog, you can build a custom application, deploy it to the SAP S/4HANA Cloud environment, integrate it with the SAP Identity and Access Management (IAM) framework, and expose it through the SAP Fiori Launchpad. Understanding the complete flow—from backend service creation to frontend deployment and authorization setup—helps accelerate custom application development while ensuring a secure and consistent user experience.

I hope this blog helps you get started with RAP-based application development and deployment in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. Feel free to share your feedback, questions, or experiences in the comments section.

entry.title: SAP Business Application Studio Integration with SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition
entry.content:
Introduction:

SAP Business Application Studio (BAS) is a development environment that provides the tools required to build SAP Fiori and SAPUI5 applications.

When developing custom applications for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, SAP Business Application Studio can be integrated with the SAP S/4HANA Cloud tenant to enable developers to access the required services and use them during application development.

This blog provides a step-by-step guide to setting up the integration between SAP Business Application Studio and SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

The setup covers the required trust configuration, SAP Business Application Studio setup, connectivity between BAS and the SAP S/4HANA Cloud tenant, and creation of a Dev Space for SAP Fiori application development.

The steps described in this blog are based on the SAP documentation:

The integration setup consists of the following steps:

SAP Cloud Identity Services
↓
SAP BTP Subaccount
↓
SAP Business Application Studio
↓
SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition Tenant
↓
SAP Fiori Dev Space

In this blog, we will cover the following topics:

  • Set Up Trust Between SAP Cloud Identity Services and SAP BTP Subaccount (Set the "Subject Identifier Name" in Step 5 to "Email")
  • Set Up SAP Business Application Studio for Development
  • Connect SAP Business Application Studio and SAP S/4HANA Cloud Tenant
  • Create a Dev Space for SAP Fiori Apps

Step 1: Set Up Trust Between SAP Cloud Identity Services and SAP BTP Subaccount

The first step is to establish trust between SAP Cloud Identity Services and the SAP BTP subaccount.

This trust configuration enables users to authenticate when accessing applications and services in the SAP BTP environment.

Navigate to the relevant SAP BTP subaccount and open the Security → Trust Configuration section.

Configure the required trust relationship with SAP Cloud Identity Services according to your landscape.

Refer to Set Up Trust Between SAP Cloud Identity Services and SAP BTP Subaccount (Set the "Subject Identifier Name" in Step 5 to "Email")

Step 2: Set Up SAP Business Application Studio for Development

After establishing the trust configuration, the next step is to set up SAP Business Application Studio in the SAP BTP subaccount.

SAP Business Application Studio is provided as a service in SAP BTP and must be subscribed to before it can be used for application development.

Refer to Set Up SAP Business Application Studio for Development

Step 3: Connect SAP Business Application Studio and SAP S/4HANA Cloud Tenant

After SAP Business Application Studio is available, the next step is to establish the connection to the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition tenant.

This connection allows SAP Business Application Studio to access the required SAP S/4HANA Cloud services during application development.

The connection can be configured using the appropriate destination configuration in the SAP BTP subaccount.

The destination represents the SAP S/4HANA Cloud tenant and provides the connection information required by SAP Business Application Studio.

Refer to Connect SAP Business Application Studio and SAP S/4HANA Cloud Tenant

Step 4: Create a Dev Space for SAP Fiori Apps

Once SAP Business Application Studio is set up and the connection to the SAP S/4HANA Cloud tenant is available, the next step is to create a Dev Space for SAP Fiori application development.

A Dev Space provides an isolated development environment containing the tools and extensions required for a specific development scenario.

Refer to Create a Dev Space for SAP Fiori Apps

entry.title: Warranty Checks on Customer Returns for High-Volume, Low-Value Products in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public
entry.content:
Dear SAP Community,

I would like to share some knowledge on warranty checks for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. Through my research, I couldn't find a direct solution for products managed in high volumes and low value. The standard scope item (63Y) is mainly targeted at heavy machinery and high-value equipment, so implementing that approach for our case would just be a headache. Nevertheless, here is what I found.

As of SAP Public Cloud release 2608, I found no standard way to assign warranties to serial numbers in bulk. This is the main reason we are going to look at two alternative approaches today, covering the pros and cons of each and how to execute them in the system.

Here are two posts I published during my research which confirm the warranty check limitations in SAP Public Cloud:

  • Warranty determination by country for serialized products

  • Reading serial numbers in the returns BAdI

The Solutions

  1. Custom Logic on the returns BAdI: Automatically checks warranty at the moment the returns order is created.

  2. A serial-level warranty report: Built using a Custom CDS View and a Custom Analytical Query.

The first approach works well until an order item ships in partial deliveries. The second handles partial deliveries smoothly, but it serves as an informational tool for the returns clerk rather than enforcing a hard block in the order.

The Requirement

Our products were serialized, low in value, and maintained in large volumes. The business rules were simple:

  • Start Date: Warranty runs from the date the unit was shipped to the customer (the actual goods issue date of its outbound delivery).

  • Duration: Depends on the country, keyed by the shipping Sales Organization (e.g., 730 days for one country, 365 days for others).

  • In-Warranty: Unit is accepted and replaced free of charge.

  • Out-of-Warranty: Unit is rejected and the customer needs to purchase a new one.

Approach 1: Custom Logic on the Returns BAdI

This approach checks warranty when the returns order is created. It uses Custom Logic on BAdI SD_SLS_MODIFY_RETURNS_ITEM (method CHANGE_RETURN_DATA) and requires the returns order to be created with reference to the original sales order.

How It Works

  1. Filter: Skip anything that isn't a standard return (CBAR).

  2. Check Reference: If there is no reference document, set the returns processing block (retsmgmtprocessingblock = 'X') and stop, since there is no shipment date to reference.

  3. Find GI Date: Read the latest actual goods issue date (ActualGoodsMovementDate) from outbound deliveries (type LF) that reference the preceding order item.

  4. Evaluate Date:

    • No GI found: Set processing block.

    • Out of warranty: If days elapsed exceed the warranty limit, set follow-up activity 0013 (Product Remains at Customer Site), populate inspection data, and set the processing block.

    • In warranty: Set follow-up activity 0001 (Receive into Plant).

The Code ABAP

CONSTANTS: lc_warranty_days    TYPE i VALUE 730,
           lc_fua_in_warranty  TYPE c LENGTH 4 VALUE '0001',
           lc_fua_out_warranty TYPE c LENGTH 4 VALUE '0013',
           lc_inspection_code  TYPE c LENGTH 4 VALUE '0001'.

IF customerreturn-salesdocumenttype <> 'CBAR'.
  RETURN.
ENDIF.

IF customerreturn-referencesddocument IS INITIAL.
  customerreturnitem_out-retsmgmtprocessingblock = 'X'.
  RETURN.
ENDIF.

SELECT MAX( dd~ActualGoodsMovementDate )
  FROM I_DeliveryDocumentItem WITH PRIVILEGED ACCESS AS di
  INNER JOIN I_DeliveryDocument WITH PRIVILEGED ACCESS AS dd
    ON dd~DeliveryDocument = di~DeliveryDocument
  WHERE di~ReferenceSDDocument     = @customerreturn-referencesddocument
    AND di~ReferenceSDDocumentItem = @customerreturnitem_in-referencesddocumentitem
    AND dd~DeliveryDocumentType    = 'LF'
  INTO @DATA(lv_gi_date).

IF lv_gi_date IS INITIAL.
  customerreturnitem_out-retsmgmtprocessingblock = 'X'.

ELSEIF cl_abap_context_info=>get_system_date( ) - lv_gi_date > lc_warranty_days.
  customerreturnitem_out-custretitmfollowupactivity    = lc_fua_out_warranty.
  customerreturnitem_out-productisinspectedatcustsite  = abap_true.
  customerreturnitem_out-returnsinspectioncode         = lc_inspection_code.
  customerreturnitem_out-returnsinspectioncomment      =
    |Out of warranty. GI { lv_gi_date DATE = USER }, limit { lc_warranty_days } days.|.
  customerreturnitem_out-retsmgmtprocessingblock       = 'X'.

ELSE.
  customerreturnitem_out-custretitmfollowupactivity = lc_fua_in_warranty.
ENDIF.

Limitations of Approach 1

This approach works perfectly—unless you issue multiple deliveries for a sales order. Due to a limitation in SD_SLS_MODIFY_RETURNS_ITEM, it fails to read individual serial numbers and can only inspect the overall outbound delivery document. We can only pick either the first or last delivery document date, which introduces inaccuracies if an order was partially shipped across multiple dates. However, if your business process always fulfills sales orders in one complete delivery, this approach is clean and automated.

Note: I have submitted a Customer Influence request for this limitation. If you face the same issue, please consider voting here: SAP Customer Influence Campaign Link.

Approach 2: A Serial-Level Warranty Report

To handle partial deliveries correctly, we must date each serial number individually rather than the overall sales order item. Every serialized unit records the exact delivery that carried it, and that delivery records when the goods issue was posted.

The relationship uses released CDS views:

I_SerialNumberDeliveryDocument (serial → delivery item) ➔ _DeliveryDocument ➔ I_DeliveryDocument.ActualGoodsMovementDate

Custom CDS View Setup

In the Custom CDS Views app, create a view with scenario Analytical Cube and primary data source I_SerialNumberDeliveryDocument:

ElementPath / CalculationPurpose
SerialNumber, Material, Equipment, DeliveryDocument, DeliveryDocumentItemDirectKey fields
ActualGoodsMovementDate_DeliveryDocumentWarranty Start Date
DeliveryDocumentType_DeliveryDocumentFilter (LF)
SalesOrganization_DeliveryDocumentDetermines warranty duration
ReferenceSDDocument, ReferenceSDDocumentItem_DeliveryDocumentItemOriginal Sales Order (for lookup)
SerialCountCalculation (Sum = 1)Cube measure
WarrantyEndDateExpression (see below)Expiration date

Warranty End Date Calculation

The warranty end date adds duration based on the Sales Organization:

SQL
DATS_ADD_DAYS($projection.ActualGoodsMovementDate,
  CASE $projection.SalesOrganization
    WHEN '1710' THEN 730
    ELSE 365
  END,
'NULL')

Since there are already many posts explaining how to create analytical reports in SAP S/4HANA Cloud, I won't go into basic report setup. Below is a preview of the final report, where the Sales Organization determines the warranty duration from the actual goods issue date:

Conclusion

Standard warranty functions in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition assume low-volume, high-value assets maintained individually. For high-volume, low-value items, both methods above derive warranty coverage dynamically from shipping events so that nothing has to be maintained per unit.

  • Custom Logic on BAdI SD_SLS_MODIFY_RETURNS_ITEM gives you an automated, enforced warranty check—ideal if each order item ships in a single delivery.

  • Custom CDS View on I_SerialNumberDeliveryDocument gives you exact, unit-level accuracy when partial deliveries are involved.

If you've solved this differently—especially if you found a way to read serial numbers inside the returns BAdI—I'd love to hear about it

References

  • SAP Community Q&A: Reading serial numbers in SD_SLS_MODIFY_RETURNS_ITEM

  • SAP Community Q&A: Warranty determination by country for serialized products

  • SAP Customer Influence Improvement Request

  • How to use Cloud BAdI to modify returns item data (SAP Community)

  • Warranty Claim Management – Customer Claim Processing in S/4HANA Cloud ERP, Public Edition (SAP Community)

Best regards,

Faisal Maayeh

Special thanks to @Chris1973  and @ElenaPuica for providing valuable insights and guidance across the Q&A threads that made this blog post possible.

entry.title: Enrichment of Solution Order Output with Information from Related Transactions Made Possible
entry.content:
Table of Contents

  • Table of Contents
  • Introduction
  • Consider an Example
  • Getting Started
  • How to Set This Up for Solution Order Output?
  • Step 1: Define Your Fields
  • Step 2: Write the Calculation Logic
  • Step 3: Create a Custom Form
  • Step 3: See Your Fields in Action
  • Key Benefits
  • Benefit
  • What It Means
  • What You Can v/s Cannot Do
  • What Works Well
  • Points to Note
  • Best Practices
  • Conclusion

 

Introduction

When you create solution orders and generate output documents like order acknowledgements or invoices, you sometimes need to show information that is not stored in the database. Instead, you want to compute it based on other fields or data from related documents.

For example, you might want to display:

  • Pricing information from follow-on sales orders
  • Data from other business documents linked to the order
  • Information from custom business tables/CDS views
  • Special calculations based on order data

Consider an Example

Imagine a company that sells software solutions. When they create an order acknowledgement, they want to show:

  • The main order information (already in the system)
  • Special pricing discounts based on customer type (calculated field)
  • Expected delivery dates from linked sales orders (calculated field)
  • Processing agents’ contact information (calculated field)

Previously, the only solution was to create permanent custom fields in the database and store the calculated data there. But this wastes database space because you only need this information on the printed output.

Data Source extension and Calculated fields in that solve this problem.

Without this, customers would need to manually create custom database fields.

With data source extension and calculated fields, this information is computed only when printing the order acknowledgement. No database clutter, and your system stays focused on core business data.

 

Getting Started

What is a Data Source Extension?

A Data Source Extension lets you bring additional fields, either from existing data or calculated on the fly, into a user interface or output form, without changing the underlying database structure.

What are Calculated Fields?

They are temporary fields that the system computes on demand when generating an output form. The data is never stored in the database, so you save space and keep your system efficient.

To extend a data source of your solution order output forms, you need:

  • Access to the Custom Fields application in your system
  • Extensibility Expert and Configuration Expert - Business Process Configuration permissions
  • Basic knowledge of ABAP programming (for writing the calculation logic)
  • An existing solution order with output management already configured
  • Adobe LiveCycle Designer

The Process: You create a data source extension, define your fields, implement the calculation logic, define a custom for template, edit the form template to add calculated fields to the print form, upload the modified print form, assign the custom form template to the Solution Order application and test in print preview. Typically, this takes 3-4 hours.

 

How to Set This Up for Solution Order Output?

 Data Source Extensions work through three simple steps:

Step 1: Define Your Fields

Using the Custom Fields application, you create a "Data Source Extension" and define what calculated fields you need and publish. For each field, you specify:

  • Field name (what you'll call it)
  • Field type (text, number, date, currency, etc.)
  • Whether it's for the header or item level

Check: Data Source Extension is created successfully and status is "Published".

Check: The calculated fields are visible in the extension.

Step 2: Write the Calculation Logic

Next, once published you see the system creates a "BAdI Implementation" for your that calculates the field values. Implement the logic to assign a value to the calculated field you created in the previous step.

This program:

  • Receives the solution order data when a form is generated
  • Performs lookups or calculations using that data
  • Fills in the calculated field values
  • Returns the results to the form

Check: Custom Logic implementation has status "Published".

Check: No syntax errors in the BAdI Implementation.

Important: This program can only read data, not modify or save anything.

It's purely a calculation engine.

Step 3: Create a Custom Form

Create a custom form template using the Maintain Form Templates (F1434) application by copying the standard form template. Edit the standard form template using Adobe LiveCycle Designer.

The calculated fields appear in SrvcDocItemExtension entity for item fields and SrvcDocHeaderExtension for header fields in the data view.

Assign the custom form template to the output type BUSINESS_SOLUTION_ORDER

https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_S4HANA_ONPREMISE/8308e6d301d54584a33cd04a9861bc52/a5817657a11a0522e10000000a44147b.html?locale=en-US&state=TEST&version=2022.002

Step 3: See Your Fields in Action

When you generate a print preview or output form for a solution order, the system automatically calculates your custom fields and displays them on the form.

Hint: You can also use Manage Output Items (F2279)” Fiori application to trigger sending output for multiple Solution Orders at once. Additionally, if you want to schedule output for one or more than one Solution Orders based on certain conditions, you could do so using the “Schedule Output for Solution Orders (F9487)” Fiori application (available in 2608 or later).

 

 Key Benefits

 

Benefit

What It Means

Save Database Space

Data is calculated when needed, not stored permanently in the database

Flexible and Powerful

Pull data from other documents, tables, or perform complex calculations

No Database Quota Used

Calculated fields don't count against your system's extension field limits

Output Only

These fields appear only on printed forms i.e. they don't affect other apps or APIs

Easy to Maintain

Changing calculation logic doesn't require database migrations

 

What You Can v/s Cannot Do

What Works Well

  • Display text, numbers, dates, and currency amounts
  • Include information from related documents or tables
  • Perform calculations and lookups
  • Use in print preview and output forms
  • Show data from custom business tables

Points to Note

Read-Only: The calculation program will not modify, create, or save any business data.

Output Only: These fields appear only on printed forms. They don't show up in other apps, reports, or APIs.

No Filtering or Searching: You cannot search or filter orders by calculated field values.

Limited Field Types: Only text and numeric field types are supported. Currency amounts support up to 2 decimal places.

Not for Analytics: Calculated fields cannot be used in analytical queries or reporting views.

 

Best Practices

Performance First: Always design your calculations to work efficiently with large batches of data. The system sends all records to your calculation program at once.

Focus on Display: Use calculated fields only for information that needs to appear on forms. Don't try to use them for filtering, searching, or reporting.

Keep Logic Simple: Complex calculations might slow down form generation. Test your calculations with real data volumes.

Document Your Fields: Clearly name and describe your calculated fields so other team members understand what they contain.

 

Conclusion

Make use of data source extension feature to enhance your solution order output forms without compromising system efficiency.
